00001: #!/bin/bash
00002: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
00003: # Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
00004: #
00005: # raofflineproxy-ctl - the backend of the OFFLINE RETROACHIEVEMENTS toggle
00006: # (fork #165; D-RA-001, D-RA-002). One system-wide switch, off by default:
00007: #
00008: #   enable   write the on-marker the unit conditions on, start the service,
00009: #            then in system.cfg record the hardcore setting as it was
00010: #            (once -- a second enable keeps the first record), turn hardcore
00011: #            off and set the toggle -- the toggle last, each write read back
00012: #            before the next, and a step that does not hold undoes every
00013: #            step this run made before it (audit #186 PL-16): a failed
00014: #            enable leaves the device exactly as it was, the toggle off. The
00015: #            proxy is casual-only and refuses hardcore awards, so the switch
00016: #            is made here, on purpose, with the sentence on screen in
00017: #            EmulationStation -- never silently.
00018: #   disable  clear the toggle, stop a scan or top-up still running (it is
00019: #            signalled through the pid in its lock file and given STOP_WAIT
00020: #            seconds; #186 PL-30), stop the service, remove the marker, and
00021: #            put hardcore back the way the record says it was; the record
00022: #            goes. Each step is read back before the next uses it up: a
00023: #            toggle that will not clear stops nothing, and a hardcore that
00024: #            will not go back keeps the record for the next disable (#308
00025: #            F-RA-18).
00026: #   start    systemctl start; the marker must already be there.
00027: #   stop     systemctl stop.
00028: #   status   enabled=, marker=, service=, hardcore= on stdout; exit 0 when the
00029: #            toggle is on, 1 when off.
00030: #   pending  how many casual awards the proxy is holding for the next
00031: #            connection: the count of pending rows in its store, on one
00032: #            line; exit 0 when there is at least one, 1 when none. With the
00033: #            toggle off the answer is 0: the service is stopped, so a row
00034: #            left in the store is not on its way anywhere, and the sentence
00035: #            the count feeds ("... WILL BE SENT NEXT TIME YOU'RE CONNECTED")
00036: #            would be a promise nobody keeps. Exit 2, nothing on stdout,
00037: #            when the store could not be read -- an unknown count is never
00038: #            reported as one, so nothing is promised on its strength.
00039: #   flushed  the stamp the service leaves after a flush that sent awards
00040: #            (patches/003: "<epoch> <flushed>", once per such flush),
00041: #            printed as written and removed, exit 0; exit 1 when there is
00042: #            none, or none worth the name. Whoever asks is told once: the
00043: #            stamp is taken (renamed) before it is read, so one the service
00044: #            writes a moment later is the next caller's, and two callers
00045: #            cannot both report the same one (#186 PL-32).
00046: #
00047: #   EmulationStation asks pending as the exit sync card ends and flushed as
00048: #   the next sync card that reached the network does (fork #173, D-RA-004);
00049: #   both answers are read through CloudText, so the shapes above are the
00050: #   contract.
00051: #
00052: #   And two read-only answers for the achievements pages, which read the
00053: #   proxy's cache when the device is offline (fork #180, D-RA-009):
00054: #
00055: #   pending-ids  the signed-in account's casual awards still waiting (an
00056: #            award's request names the account that earned it; one that
00057: #            names none counts, #308 F-RA-09), one per line as
00058: #            "<achievementId> <epoch>" (when it was earned, in seconds),
00059: #            oldest first; exit 0 with at least one, 1 with none. The page
00060: #            marks those achievements as earned and waiting to be sent. The
00061: #            same refusals as pending: toggle off or no store answers
00062: #            nothing with exit 1, a store that cannot be read exit 2.
00063: #   summary  one line of JSON per game the store holds for the signed-in
00064: #            account -- id, title, icon, achievements, points, unlocked,
00065: #            unlockedPoints, pending -- from one read of sqlite: the page's
00066: #            whole offline summary without a request per game (fork #190).
00067: #            A game a launch cached (its achievementsets row, no patch row)
00068: #            is listed too, and unlocked and unlockedPoints are null when the
00069: #            game's unlock row is missing or cannot be read (#307 PL-057).
00070: #            Exit 1 with the toggle off, no account or no store; 2 when the
00071: #            store cannot be read (the reader's 3, said through cannot_tell
00072: #            as every read here says it; #308 F-RA-28).
00073: #   account  the signed-in account's points as RetroAchievements last told
00074: #            the proxy, from its cached sign-in: "score=<n> softcore=<n>" on
00075: #            one line, exit 0; exit 1 when the toggle is off, nothing is
00076: #            cached for this account, or the cached sign-in carries no
00077: #            points -- the proxy writes one without them when it signs in
00078: #            from a token rather than a password (auth.py
00079: #            cache_token_credentials), and an absent number is not 0 (#186
00080: #            PL-26); exit 2 when the store cannot be read. Reads the row
00081: #            that also holds the session token and prints the two numbers
00082: #            and nothing else.
00083: #
00084: # And the three verbs of SCAN GAMES FOR OFFLINE ACHIEVEMENTS (fork #179,
00085: # D-RA-010; fork #184, D-RA-013): the proxy serves a game offline only from
00086: # what it cached while online, so a game never started with a connection
00087: # earned nothing offline until somebody started it once online. The scan
00088: # caches every game on the console that RetroAchievements knows, and the
00089: # top-up keeps the cache following the library without anyone pressing
00090: # anything.
00091: #
00092: #   Both follow the interface's own game index (D-RA-013). INDEX NEW GAMES
00093: #   AT STARTUP and INDEX GAMES (the hasher) write each game's <cheevosHash>
00094: #   and, where RetroAchievements knows the hash, its <cheevosId> into the
00095: #   system's gamelist.xml -- through the interface's recovery/<system>/ files
00096: #   until it writes the gamelist at its next clean exit; this reads both.
00097: #   The rule, per system: where an index exists (any game with a cheevosHash)
00098: #   only the games with a cheevosId are cached, from the id and the hash the
00099: #   interface already has -- the ROM is never read again -- and the games
00100: #   without an entry are left to the index (they are the ones it found no
00101: #   set for, or the ones added since it ran, which the next index picks up);
00102: #   where no index exists at all, every ROM under the folder is hashed and
00103: #   looked up as before. So a library that was indexed never has its
00104: #   leftovers hashed one at a time on every run, and a device that never
00105: #   indexed still gets the whole scan. The work is done by
00106: #   raofflineproxy-cache-indexed beside this script, over a job list
00107: #   list_jobs writes (its header has the two line shapes).
00108: #
00109: #   scan     list the jobs (above), and hand them to the helper: an indexed
00110: #            game costs the proxy's patch, unlocks and achievementsets
00111: #            requests and no hash lookup; an unindexed one the client's own
00112: #            add_rom_to_cache (hash, gameid, then the same three). A page in
00113: #            EmulationStation (GuiOfflineScan) runs it and reads its ">>> "
00114: #            lines: `doing listing`, `total <n>`, `game <i>|<n>|<name>`,
00115: #            `cached <c>|<s>`, `note <TOKEN>`, `errors <n>`, `why <TOKEN>`,
00116: #            `done <c>|<s>|<ready>|<limit>`. Refuses -- with an exit code
00117: #            the page names and no stamp -- when the toggle is off (78), no
00118: #            account is signed in (77), the device is offline by the proxy's
00119: #            own probe (69), or another scan or top-up holds the lock (75).
00120: #            Stops after three lookups in a row that RetroAchievements did
00121: #            not answer, on a refused sign-in, or should the client ever
00122: #            report a cache limit (none on ROCKNIX since patch 004). Writes
00123: #            last-scan (below) and exits 0 when every game it tried was
00124: #            cached or passed over as one RetroAchievements does not know,
00125: #            1 when it could not finish -- and a game whose fetch failed,
00126: #            even one among many that went through, is a run that could
00127: #            not finish (`why SOME_GAMES_NOT_SAVED`, `errors <n>`; #186
00128: #            PL-24): the next scan or top-up tries those games again, since
00129: #            nothing marks them cached. Every scan ends with the image pass
00130: #            (a scan with nothing new included), and a pass that left
00131: #            images behind makes the scan one that could not finish too,
00132: #            `why SOME_IMAGES_NOT_SAVED` (#307 PL-060; a top-up that cached
00133: #            a game runs it and says it the same way). The walk over an unindexed folder
00134: #            stops at the client's cap of files (rom_browser
00135: #            MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES), counted over the files not yet cached and
00136: #            begun where the last walk the cap cut stopped (scan-cursor,
00137: #            kept only by a run that worked through its jobs), so
00138: #            a second scan reaches what the first did not, past files that
00139: #            never cache too (#186 PL-17, #307 PL-059); a walk the cap cut
00140: #            says `note TRUNCATED` to the page and truncated=1 in the stamp.
00141: #   topup    every game the index knows and the client has not cached, then
00142: #            the client's `run-smart-cache` (RetroArch's recent history,
00143: #            PPSSPP's recent list) for what the index missed -- so a game
00144: #            added and indexed, or played once online, is cached even if the
00145: #            scan was never pressed. For EmulationStation's network-up hook:
00146: #            silent (nothing on stdout), bounded -- one attempt per half
00147: #            hour, and one deadline of TOPUP_TIMEOUT seconds from the moment
00148: #            it starts that the wait for the lock, the probes, the listing
00149: #            and both passes all spend from (#186 PL-28); a first top-up over
00150: #            a library nobody scanned caches what fits and the next connect
00151: #            carries on -- the same refusals as scan with the same codes,
00152: #            and it writes last-scan only when it cached something or could
00153: #            not finish; a top-up that found nothing new leaves the last
00154: #            scan's line alone. The hook fires when the address arrives,
00155: #            which on a hotspot is before its resolver answers (#175), so
00156: #            the probe has the token check's patience: up to PROBE_TRIES
00157: #            tries PROBE_INTERVAL seconds apart, inside the deadline. The
00158: #            half-hour mark is set only once a probe has reached
00159: #            RetroAchievements -- a probe that could not is no attempt, and
00160: #            the next link event tries again (#186 PL-04).
00161: #   topup --after-index
00162: #            the same, started by EmulationStation as its hasher finishes
00163: #            with the toggle on: the index has just grown, so this one does
00164: #            not count the half hour since the last attempt against itself,
00165: #            and it waits for a top-up already running rather than giving
00166: #            way to one that read the index before it grew -- the wait
00167: #            spending from the same deadline.
00168: #   index-offline
00169: #            EmulationStation's index had games to identify and the hash
00170: #            library did not come: leaves index-pending, the marker the
00171: #            after-index run leaves when its probe fails, so the next
00172: #            link-return topup lists the library once (fork #299, D-UI-104).
00173: #            No probe; exit 0. What that listing can find is the games the
00174: #            index did identify -- the case the after-index run's marker is
00175: #            for. The games this index could not identify have no
00176: #            cheevosId yet, so no listing finds them: what caches them is
00177: #            the interface running its index again when the link comes up
00178: #            (NetworkThread, while the hash library has not come this
00179: #            session and INDEX NEW GAMES AT STARTUP is on) and the topup
00180: #            --after-index that follows it (#308 F-RA-22).
00181: #   listening [--wait N]
00182: #            whether something takes an IPv4 connection to 127.0.0.1:8080, the
00183: #            proxy's address -- a listener on it in LISTEN: exit 0
00184: #            when it is, 1 when not -- read from /proc/net/tcp and tcp6, no
00185: #            tool run. With --wait it looks N times a second apart. The
00186: #            unit's ExecStartPost, so the service is started when it can be
00187: #            reached, not when its process has forked (#308 F-RA-26).
00188: #   ready    how many games are cached: the count in the client's own
00189: #            cached_game_ids.txt export (one id per line, rewritten on every
00190: #            cache change by the service and the client alike), on one line.
00191: #
00192: #   running  /storage/.config/raofflineproxy/running while a scan or top-up is
00193: #            at its jobs (fork #189): one line, `route=<scan|topup> at=<epoch>
00194: #            [index=<i> total=<n> name=<game>]`, rewritten as each game
00195: #            finishes (index is the game it is on now), removed when the
00196: #            run ends -- the interface shows a run it did not start from it,
00197: #            and treats one older than the bound as gone.
00198: #   last-scan is /storage/.config/raofflineproxy/last-scan, one line:
00199: #   "<epoch> <rc> <scan|topup> cached=<n> skipped=<m> ready=<total>
00200: #   limit=<0|1> indexed=<i> errors=<e> added=<k>[ truncated=1][ why=<TOKEN>][ note=<TOKEN>]" -- how
00201: #   the last run went, read by the page for the line under the row
00202: #   (CloudText::parseScanStamp, which passes over keys it does not know). A
00203: #   scan that found no game to look at is rc 0 with note=NO_GAMES (fork
00204: #   #329): a run with nothing to do completed.
00205: #   `added` is how many games the run made ready for this account (fork
00206: #   #298), read from the store before and after -- a game is ready with the
00207: #   account's unlocks row and an achievementsets row of the game (audit of
00208: #   the fixes, claude G-D-08) -- rather than counted from the run's cache
00209: #   operations: a game the recently played pass (the client's
00210: #   run-smart-cache, which takes only games not yet cached) caches for the
00211: #   first time is added, and a second dump of a game already ready is
00212: #   cached but not added (#308 F-RA-10, F-RA-15). The card says "added" of
00213: #   those and "ready" otherwise. When the store could not be read before or
00214: #   after a run that cached games, added=unknown: a count nobody measured
00215: #   is never written as one (PL-031).
00216: #   `skipped` is the ROMs RetroAchievements does not know, which the client
00217: #   refuses one at a time and the scan counts rather than reports (the
00218: #   proxy's own docs skip them silently); `indexed` is how many of `cached`
00219: #   came from the interface's index without a hash; `errors` is how many
00220: #   games a fetch failed for, which is what makes rc 1 with
00221: #   why=SOME_GAMES_NOT_SAVED; a scan the player cancelled from its page
00222: #   (SIGINT from the interface, D-UI-078) is rc 130 with why=CANCELLED and
00223: #   the counts it had reached. Tokens, never sentences: the page says them
00224: #   in the player's language. scan.log beside it carries the helper's line for
00225: #   every game -- which RetroAchievements actions it cost, so an indexed
00226: #   game shows patch,unlocks,achievementsets and never gameid; the client
00227: #   redacts the token in what it logs and prints file names and reasons
00228: #   only, and nothing here prints a value from system.cfg.
00229: #
00230: # The toggle is global.retroachievements.offlineproxy in system.cfg, the
00231: # setting setsettings.sh (RetroArch) and cheevos_ppsspp.sh read at every
00232: # launch to point the emulator at 127.0.0.1:8080 -- into that launch's own
00233: # config, so no host ever lands in a file a settings backup carries.
00234: # system.cfg travels with the toggle in it; the marker under /storage/.cache
00235: # does not, and /usr/lib/autostart/daemons/006-raofflineproxy re-derives it
00236: # at boot. Everything the proxy itself writes lives under
00237: # /storage/.config/raofflineproxy, which backuptool holds back whole (its
00238: # token cache and award queue never travel, D-INFRA-010).
00239: #
00240: # The store this reads -- read-only, through the service's own sqlite3
00241: # module, never written here -- is the client's schema at the commit
00242: # package.mk pins (c7ebd1b6e777f3751ff0ecdf8aba54045844e00d, storage.py
00243: # _initialize_sqlite, reviewed 2026-10-11 for #541). Consumed columns and
00244: # cache-key spellings remain compatible. The additive cached_game_meta table
00245: # and delete/rename triggers index existing rows without changing award data. The suite reads a store the current client wrote,
00246: # and the integration fixture reopens the predecessor's store with current
00247: # Storage twice, preserving cache/login/base/subset award bytes: pending_awards(id,
00248: # achievementId, queryString, requestBody, queuedAt, status) for pending,
00249: # pending-ids and summary; api_cache(cacheKey, responseBody, sourceRomPath,
00250: # cachedAt) for account, summary, the ready set behind added= and the
00251: # scan's "already cached" test, the keys as cache_keys.py spells them
00252: # (login2::<user>, patch:<id>:<user>, unlocks:<id>:<user>:0,
00253: # achievementsets:<hash>:<user>). The client carries no schema version row
00254: # (an upstream item, #186 PL-22); a schema it changes shows here as
00255: # cannot_tell (exit 2), never as a number -- and first in the scripts
00256: # suite, which runs these reads against a store the pinned client's own
00257: # Storage wrote and checks that this paragraph names the pin package.mk
00258: # pins, so a pin that moves makes somebody read the schema again.
00259: 
00260: # Machine-facing. The last line of stdout after enable or disable is
00261: # hardcore=<0|1>, the setting as it stands afterwards; EmulationStation
00262: # reads it to keep its HARDCORE MODE row truthful. Everything else goes to
00263: # the log. Exit 0 when done, 1 when a step could not be made to hold, 2 on
00264: # usage or when an answer could not be read; scan and topup add the four
00265: # sysexits codes above, which CloudExit.h in EmulationStation spells the
00266: # same way.
00267: 
00268: # No set -u: get_setting and set_setting come from /etc/profile and read
00269: # positional parameters they were not given; every value this script relies
00270: # on is read back and tested below instead.
00271: . /etc/profile
00272: 
00273: MARKER_DIR="/storage/.cache/services"
00274: MARKER="${MARKER_DIR}/raofflineproxy.conf"
00275: UNIT="raofflineproxy.service"
00276: KEY="global.retroachievements.offlineproxy"
00277: HARDCORE_KEY="global.retroachievements.hardcore"
00278: HARDCORE_WAS_KEY="global.retroachievements.offlineproxy.hardcore_was"
00279: # Where the service keeps everything it writes: RAOFFLINEPROXY_CONFIG_DIR in
00280: # the unit, and the default the proxy resolves on a ROCKNIX image without it.
00281: PROXY_DIR="/storage/.config/raofflineproxy"
00282: QUEUE="${PROXY_DIR}/proxy.sqlite3"
00283: FLUSH_STAMP="${PROXY_DIR}/last-flush"
00284: 
00285: # The scan's files, all beside the proxy's own so backuptool holds them back
00286: # with the rest (D-INFRA-010) and `disable` leaves them where the cache is.
00287: SCAN_STAMP="${PROXY_DIR}/last-scan"
00288: # Where the walk over unindexed folders stopped at the cap, so the next scan
00289: # walks on from there (#307 PL-059): the path of the last file it took.
00290: SCAN_CURSOR="${PROXY_DIR}/scan-cursor"
00291: SCAN_LOG="${PROXY_DIR}/scan.log"
00292: RUNNING="${PROXY_DIR}/running"
00293: TOPUP_MARK="${PROXY_DIR}/last-topup-attempt"
00294: # An index run that could not reach RetroAchievements (a game list updated
00295: # offline) leaves this, and the next link-return run lists the library
00296: # once for it, so the games an index identified while the device was
00297: # offline are cached when it is next online (fork #299; the games an index
00298: # could not identify are the interface's next index's, #308 F-RA-22). It is
00299: # removed only by a run whose listing and indexed pass both went through, so
00300: # a run that fails or is stopped part-way leaves it for the next (#307
00301: # PL-055).
00302: INDEX_PENDING="${PROXY_DIR}/index-pending"
00303: READY_FILE="${PROXY_DIR}/cached_game_ids.txt"
00304: SCAN_LOCK="/var/run/raofflineproxy-scan.lock"
00305: ROMS_ROOT="/storage/roms"
00306: # The interface's own folder: es_systems.cfg, and the two places its game
00307: # index is kept on disk (gamelists/<system>/ and recovery/<system>/).
00308: ES_DIR="/storage/.config/emulationstation"
00309: # The account keys EmulationStation writes (the token after a sign-in). Read
00310: # for presence only, never printed.
00311: USER_KEY="global.retroachievements.username"
00312: TOKEN_KEY="global.retroachievements.token"
00313: PASSWORD_KEY="global.retroachievements.password"
00314: 
00315: # sysexits.h, as CloudExit.h names them: a run that did nothing, and why.
00316: EX_USAGE=64         # a bad argument; the usage line was printed (refresh, audit #258 PL-012)
00317: EX_UNAVAILABLE=69   # offline by the proxy's probe
00318: EX_TEMPFAIL=75      # another scan or top-up holds the lock
00319: EX_NOPERM=77        # no RetroAchievements account signed in
00320: EX_CONFIG=78        # the toggle is off
00321: 
00322: # The top-up's probe schedule: the token check's (#175, CheevosRetry.h --
00323: # nine tries ten seconds apart), for the same reason: the hook fires when
00324: # the address arrives, and a hotspot's resolver answers 20-45 s later.
00325: PROBE_TRIES=9
00326: PROBE_INTERVAL=10
00327: # How long disable waits for a scan or top-up it has asked to stop.
00328: STOP_WAIT=10
00329: # Lookups RetroAchievements did not answer, in a row, before the scan stops
00330: # asking: every one is a request spent on a link or a sign-in that is not
00331: # working, and the page can say so sooner.
00332: ERRORS_IN_A_ROW=3
00333: # One automatic top-up attempt per this many seconds, and no single run
00334: # longer than TOPUP_TIMEOUT: a link that flaps must not turn into a request
00335: # storm, and a hook that never returns is a hook nobody can reason about.
00336: TOPUP_INTERVAL=1800
00337: TOPUP_TIMEOUT=900
00338: 
00339: # The client resolves its folder the way the unit sets it, and RetroArch's
00340: # `~` in content_history_path and playlist_directory is /storage on ROCKNIX
00341: # (the proxy expands it with HOME, and EmulationStation's may differ).
00342: export RAOFFLINEPROXY_CONFIG_DIR="${PROXY_DIR}"
00343: export HOME=/storage
00344: export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/storage/.config
00345: PROXY_PY="python3 -m raofflineproxy.main"
00346: 
00347: # The ROCKNIX ROM folders of the systems RetroAchievements has sets for, by
00348: # RetroAchievements' console list (2026-09) mapped onto the folder names
00349: # es_systems.cfg uses on this image, both spellings where two images differ
00350: # (coleco/colecovision, odyssey/odyssey2, pc88/pc-8800, fbneo/fbn,
00351: # sgfx/supergrafx). A folder that is not here is never walked: the proxy
00352: # would only hash it and be told no, one request per file, and a computer
00353: # or Windows library can be tens of gigabytes. Arcade folders hash by file
00354: # name (rc_hash's arcade rule), so they cost no reading. The hack folders
00355: # (nesh, snesh, ...) stay: RetroAchievements has sets for many hacks, and
00356: # the ones it does not know are skipped like any other ROM.
00357: SCAN_SYSTEMS="
00358:   nes famicom fds nesh snes sfc snesh snesmsu1 satellaview sufami
00359:   gb gbh gbc gbch gba gbah n64 n64dd nds ndsiware gamecube wii
00360:   pokemini virtualboy megaduck supervision arduboy wasm4 uzebox
00361:   channelf odyssey odyssey2 videopac intellivision coleco colecovision vectrex
00362:   mastersystem megadrive genesis megadrive-japan megadriveh genh sega32x
00363:   segacd megacd saturn dreamcast gamegear gamegearh ggh sg-1000
00364:   psx ps2 psp pspminis
00365:   atari2600 atari7800 atarijaguar atarijaguarcd atarilynx
00366:   pcengine tg16 pcenginecd tg16cd sgfx supergrafx pcfx pc88 pc-8800
00367:   ngp ngpc neocd wonderswan wonderswancolor msx msx2 amstradcpc apple2 3do
00368:   arcade mame fbneo fbn neogeo cps1 cps2 cps3
00369: "
00370: 
00371: say() {
00372:     logger -t raofflineproxy-ctl "$*"
00373: }
00374: 
00375: fail() {
00376:     say "$*"
00377:     echo "raofflineproxy-ctl: $*" >&2
00378:     exit 1
00379: }
00380: 
00381: # A setting as system.cfg holds it; empty when absent.
00382: setting() {
00383:     get_setting "${1}"
00384: }
00385: 
00386: # 0 or 1, from a value that may be empty or anything else.
00387: as_flag() {
00388:     if [ "${1:-}" = "1" ]; then echo 1; else echo 0; fi
00389: }
00390: 
00391: have_systemctl() {
00392:     command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1
00393: }
00394: 
00395: service_state() {
00396:     if have_systemctl; then
00397:         systemctl is-active "${UNIT}" 2>/dev/null || true
00398:     else
00399:         echo unknown
00400:     fi
00401: }
00402: 
00403: do_start() {
00404:     have_systemctl || fail "no systemctl to start ${UNIT} with"
00405:     systemctl start "${UNIT}" || fail "${UNIT} did not start"
00406: }
00407: 
00408: do_stop() {
00409:     have_systemctl || return 0
00410:     systemctl stop "${UNIT}" || say "${UNIT} did not stop cleanly; carrying on"
00411: }
00412: 
00413: # What this run of enable changed, for enable_undo to put back: the marker
00414: # and the service only when this run made or started them (a second enable
00415: # finds both in place and leaves them), the record only when this run wrote
00416: # it, and each setting's value from before the run.
00417: E_MARKER_WAS=0; E_SERVICE_WAS=0; E_STARTED=0; E_RECORD_WROTE=0
00418: E_HARDCORE_BEFORE=""; E_HARDCORE_CHANGED=0; E_KEY_BEFORE=""; E_KEY_CHANGED=0
00419: 
00420: # A setting back to what it was: its old value, or gone when it had none.
00421: put_back() {
00422:     if [ -n "${2}" ]; then set_setting "${1}" "${2}"; else set_setting "${1}" default; fi
00423: }
00424: 
00425: # A step of enable did not hold: undo every step this run made, in the
00426: # order that keeps the device consistent at each point -- the toggle first
00427: # (the launchers and the boot pass read it and nothing else), the settings,
00428: # then the service and the marker -- and fail. A device on which enable
00429: # failed is a device on which enable never ran (#186 PL-16).
00430: enable_undo() {
00431:     say "enable: $*; putting the device back as it was"
00432:     [ "${E_KEY_CHANGED}" -eq 1 ] && put_back "${KEY}" "${E_KEY_BEFORE}"
00433:     [ "${E_HARDCORE_CHANGED}" -eq 1 ] && put_back "${HARDCORE_KEY}" "${E_HARDCORE_BEFORE}"
00434:     [ "${E_RECORD_WROTE}" -eq 1 ] && set_setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}" default
00435:     [ "${E_STARTED}" -eq 1 ] && [ "${E_SERVICE_WAS}" -eq 0 ] && do_stop
00436:     [ "${E_MARKER_WAS}" -eq 0 ] && rm -f "${MARKER}"
00437:     fail "$*"
00438: }
00439: 
00440: do_enable() {
00441:     E_KEY_BEFORE="$(setting "${KEY}")"
00442:     E_HARDCORE_BEFORE="$(setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}")"
00443:     [ -e "${MARKER}" ] && E_MARKER_WAS=1
00444:     [ "$(service_state)" = "active" ] && E_SERVICE_WAS=1
00445: 
00446:     # The marker first, the service second: if the service cannot start,
00447:     # nothing about the player's settings has changed yet, and the marker
00448:     # goes again so the next boot does not start what could not run now.
00449:     mkdir -p "${MARKER_DIR}" || fail "cannot create ${MARKER_DIR}"
00450:     touch "${MARKER}" || fail "cannot write ${MARKER}"
00451:     if have_systemctl; then
00452:         if ! systemctl start "${UNIT}"; then
00453:             [ "${E_MARKER_WAS}" -eq 0 ] && rm -f "${MARKER}"
00454:             fail "${UNIT} did not start; the toggle stays off"
00455:         fi
00456:         E_STARTED=1
00457:     fi
00458: 
00459:     # Then the settings, each read back before the next is written, the
00460:     # toggle last of all: until it reads 1 nothing routes through the proxy,
00461:     # so a failure anywhere before it leaves the device as it was once
00462:     # enable_undo has run, and a failure after it cannot happen -- it is
00463:     # the last write.
00464:     #
00465:     # Record hardcore as it was, once. A second enable finds the record and
00466:     # keeps it, so the value disable puts back is the player's and not the 0
00467:     # the first enable wrote.
00468:     if [ -z "$(setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}")" ]; then
00469:         set_setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}" "$(as_flag "${E_HARDCORE_BEFORE}")"
00470:         E_RECORD_WROTE=1
00471:         [ -n "$(setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}")" ] || enable_undo "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY} did not take"
00472:     fi
00473:     set_setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}" 0
00474:     E_HARDCORE_CHANGED=1
00475:     [ "$(setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}")" = "0" ] || enable_undo "${HARDCORE_KEY} did not take"
00476:     set_setting "${KEY}" 1
00477:     E_KEY_CHANGED=1
00478:     [ "$(setting "${KEY}")" = "1" ] || enable_undo "${KEY} did not take"
00479:     [ -e "${MARKER}" ] || enable_undo "${MARKER} is gone"
00480: 
00481:     say "offline RetroAchievements on: hardcore was $(setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}"), now 0; ${UNIT} $(service_state)"
00482:     echo "hardcore=0"
00483: }
00484: 
00485: # A scan or top-up the interface started is no child of this process; its
00486: # lock file carries its pid (take_lock writes it), so it is asked to stop
00487: # (SIGTERM: its trap ends the helper and cleans up) and given STOP_WAIT
00488: # seconds to let go of the lock. Nothing else is matched by name or pattern.
00489: # Exit 0 when nothing was running or it stopped, 1 when it did not.
00490: stop_running_run() {
00491:     [ -e "${SCAN_LOCK}" ] || return 0
00492:     exec 7<>"${SCAN_LOCK}" || return 0
00493:     if flock -n 7; then exec 7>&-; return 0; fi
00494:     local PID WAITED=0
00495:     PID="$(head -n 1 "${SCAN_LOCK}" 2>/dev/null)"
00496:     case "${PID}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) PID="" ;; esac
00497:     if [ -n "${PID}" ]; then
00498:         say "disable: a scan or top-up is running (pid ${PID}); asking it to stop"
00499:         kill -TERM "${PID}" 2>/dev/null
00500:     else
00501:         say "disable: a scan or top-up holds the lock and left no pid; waiting for it"
00502:     fi
00503:     until flock -n 7; do
00504:         if [ "${WAITED}" -ge "${STOP_WAIT}" ]; then
00505:             say "disable: the running scan or top-up did not stop within ${STOP_WAIT}s; carrying on"
00506:             exec 7>&-
00507:             return 1
00508:         fi
00509:         sleep 1
00510:         WAITED=$((WAITED + 1))
00511:     done
00512:     exec 7>&-
00513:     say "disable: the running scan or top-up stopped"
00514:     return 0
00515: }
00516: 
00517: do_disable() {
00518:     # The toggle first: a scan or top-up starting from now on is refused by
00519:     # its own check, and the launchers route direct from the next launch.
00520:     # Each step is read back before the next one uses it up (#308 F-RA-18):
00521:     # a toggle that did not clear stops nothing, so the device stays on --
00522:     # service, marker and record together -- rather than half off.
00523:     set_setting "${KEY}" 0
00524:     [ "$(setting "${KEY}")" = "0" ] || fail "${KEY} did not clear; the service, the marker and the hardcore record are left as they were"
00525:     stop_running_run
00526:     do_stop
00527:     rm -f "${MARKER}"
00528: 
00529:     # Put hardcore back as the record says, and remove the record only once
00530:     # hardcore reads back as it says: a write that did not hold keeps the
00531:     # record, so the next disable can still put the player's setting back
00532:     # (#308 F-RA-18). No record -- a device that never had the toggle on, or
00533:     # a second disable -- leaves it alone.
00534:     local WAS
00535:     WAS="$(setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}")"
00536:     if [ -n "${WAS}" ]; then
00537:         set_setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}" "$(as_flag "${WAS}")"
00538:         [ "$(setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}")" = "$(as_flag "${WAS}")" ] || fail "${HARDCORE_KEY} was not put back; the record is kept for the next disable"
00539:         set_setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}" default
00540:         [ -z "$(setting "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY}")" ] || fail "${HARDCORE_WAS_KEY} was not cleared"
00541:     fi
00542: 
00543:     [ ! -e "${MARKER}" ] || fail "${MARKER} could not be removed"
00544: 
00545:     say "offline RetroAchievements off: hardcore ${WAS:+put back to }${WAS:-left as it was}; ${UNIT} $(service_state)"
00546:     echo "hardcore=$(as_flag "$(setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}")")"
00547: }
00548: 
00549: do_status() {
00550:     local ON
00551:     ON="$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")"
00552:     echo "enabled=${ON}"
00553:     if [ -e "${MARKER}" ]; then echo "marker=1"; else echo "marker=0"; fi
00554:     echo "service=$(service_state)"
00555:     echo "hardcore=$(as_flag "$(setting "${HARDCORE_KEY}")")"
00556:     [ "${ON}" = "1" ]
00557: }
00558: 
00559: # The count could not be read: nothing on stdout, the reason on stderr and in
00560: # the log, exit 2. A guard that cannot run has not passed -- and a number
00561: # that is not known is not printed as one.
00562: cannot_tell() {
00563:     say "$*"
00564:     echo "raofflineproxy-ctl: $*" >&2
00565:     exit 2
00566: }
00567: 
00568: do_pending() {
00569:     if [ "$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "${QUEUE}" ]; then
00570:         echo 0
00571:         return 1
00572:     fi
00573:     # The same interpreter and sqlite3 module the service writes the store
00574:     # with (the package depends on Python3 for the service itself), opened
00575:     # read-only, with a second's patience for a write in flight. The image
00576:     # also carries a sqlite3 binary, but not by this package's asking.
00577:     local N
00578:     N="$(python3 -c '
00579: import sqlite3, sys
00580: db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % sys.argv[1], uri=True, timeout=1.0)
00581: print(db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pending_awards WHERE status = ?", ("pending",)).fetchone()[0])
00582: ' "${QUEUE}" 2>/dev/null)" || cannot_tell "the award queue at ${QUEUE} could not be read"
00583:     case "${N}" in
00584:         ''|*[!0-9]*) cannot_tell "the award queue answered '${N}', not a count" ;;
00585:     esac
00586:     echo "${N}"
00587:     [ "${N}" -gt 0 ]
00588: }
00589: 
00590: # The pending awards by id, oldest first, each with the second it was earned
00591: # (the store keeps milliseconds). Read the way pending reads: read-only, the
00592: # service's own sqlite3 module, a second's patience.
00593: do_pending_ids() {
00594:     if [ "$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "${QUEUE}" ]; then
00595:         return 1
00596:     fi
00597:     # The signed-in account's awards, and those that name no account: the
00598:     # page marks these as this player's, so another account's award on this
00599:     # device is not among them (#308 gpt F-RA-09). No account set: all, as
00600:     # before.
00601:     local ROWS
00602:     ROWS="$(python3 -c '
00603: import sqlite3, sys
00604: from urllib.parse import parse_qs
00605: user = sys.argv[2].strip().lower()
00606: def owner(query, body):
00607:     for text in ((query or "").split("?", 1)[-1], body or ""):
00608:         values = parse_qs(text, keep_blank_values=True).get("u")
00609:         if values and values[0].strip():
00610:             return values[0].strip().lower()
00611:     return ""
00612: db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % sys.argv[1], uri=True, timeout=1.0)
00613: for aid, queued, query, body in db.execute("SELECT achievementId, queuedAt, queryString, requestBody FROM pending_awards WHERE status = ? ORDER BY queuedAt ASC, id ASC", ("pending",)):
00614:     if not user or owner(query, body) in ("", user):
00615:         print(int(aid), int(queued) // 1000)
00616: ' "${QUEUE}" "$(setting "${USER_KEY}")" 2>/dev/null)" || cannot_tell "the award queue at ${QUEUE} could not be read"
00617:     [ -n "${ROWS}" ] || return 1
00618:     printf '%s\n' "${ROWS}"
00619:     return 0
00620: }
00621: 
00622: # summary: the page's whole offline summary in one read of the store (fork
00623: # #190: 247 saved games were 494 requests to the service, each tried
00624: # upstream first while the service still believed it was online -- hours on
00625: # a link that had just gone). One JSON object a line, sorted by id:
00626: #   {"id":4902,"title":"Bobl","icon":"http://127.0.0.1:8080/Images/x.png",
00627: #    "achievements":12,"points":110,"unlocked":1,"unlockedPoints":5,"pending":1}
00628: # A game is the account's patch row, or -- for a game a launch cached and
00629: # nothing else did -- its achievementsets row (RetroArch asks achievementsets,
00630: # not patch; #307 PL-057), read as the interface's game page reads one: the
00631: # set of Type core, else the first. The core set (Flags 3, positive ids) as
00632: # the interface reads a patch; a game whose set is empty is not a cached game
00633: # (audit #186 PL-26); unlocked counts the store's unlocks and the casual
00634: # awards still waiting, as the service's own offline unlocks answer does --
00635: # and when the store's unlock row for the game is missing or cannot be read,
00636: # unlocked and unlockedPoints are null: unknown, never 0 (#307 PL-057). The
00637: # icon carries the service's address as the service would rewrite it. Exit
00638: # 1 with the toggle off, no account set or no store; the store that cannot
00639: # be read is a cannot_tell (exit 2).
00640: do_summary() {
00641:     if [ "$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "${QUEUE}" ]; then
00642:         return 1
00643:     fi
00644:     local USER
00645:     USER="$(setting "${USER_KEY}")"
00646:     [ -n "${USER}" ] || return 1
00647:     python3 - "${QUEUE}" "${USER}" <<'PY_SUMMARY'
00648: import json, sqlite3, sys
00649: from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
00650: store, user = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2].strip().lower()
00651: base = "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
00652: def icon_url(text):
00653:     text = (text or "").strip()
00654:     if not text:
00655:         return ""
00656:     if text.startswith("/"):
00657:         return base + text
00658:     if "://" in text:
00659:         path = urlsplit(text).path
00660:         return base + path if path else ""
00661:     return base + "/" + text
00662: def core_of(achievements):
00663:     return [a for a in (achievements or []) if isinstance(a, dict) and int(a.get("Flags") or 3) == 3 and int(a.get("ID") or 0) > 0]
00664: def set_achievements(data):
00665:     # OfflineAchievementsText::parseAchievementSets: the set of Type core, else the first.
00666:     if isinstance(data.get("Achievements"), list):
00667:         return data["Achievements"]
00668:     chosen = None
00669:     for one in data.get("Sets") or []:
00670:         if not isinstance(one, dict):
00671:             continue
00672:         if chosen is None:
00673:             chosen = one
00674:         if one.get("Type") == "core":
00675:             chosen = one
00676:             break
00677:     return (chosen or {}).get("Achievements") or []
00678: try:
00679:     db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % store, uri=True, timeout=1.0)
00680:     patches = db.execute("SELECT cacheKey, responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey LIKE ? ORDER BY cacheKey", ("patch:%:" + user,)).fetchall()
00681:     sets = db.execute("SELECT cacheKey, responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey LIKE ? ORDER BY cacheKey", ("achievementsets:%:" + user,)).fetchall()
00682:     unlock_rows = dict(db.execute("SELECT cacheKey, responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey LIKE ?", ("unlocks:%:" + user + ":0",)).fetchall())
00683:     awards = db.execute("SELECT achievementId, queryString, requestBody FROM pending_awards WHERE status = 'pending'").fetchall()
00684: except Exception:
00685:     sys.exit(3)
00686: def owner(query, body):
00687:     # The account an award was earned by: its request's u=, in the query or
00688:     # the body, as the service reads it (utils.extract_request_param).
00689:     for text in ((query or "").split("?", 1)[-1], body or ""):
00690:         values = parse_qs(text, keep_blank_values=True).get("u")
00691:         if values and values[0].strip():
00692:             return values[0].strip().lower()
00693:     return ""
00694: # Awards waiting for this account, or naming none: another account's award
00695: # on this device is that account's, not whoever is signed in now (#308 gpt
00696: # F-RA-09).
00697: pending = {int(aid) for aid, query, body in awards if owner(query, body) in ("", user)}
00698: found = {}   # id -> (title, icon, core set)
00699: for key, body in patches:
00700:     parts = key.split(":")
00701:     if len(parts) != 3 or parts[2] != user:
00702:         continue
00703:     try:
00704:         gid = int(parts[1])
00705:         patch = (json.loads(body) or {}).get("PatchData") or {}
00706:         core = core_of(patch.get("Achievements"))
00707:     except Exception:
00708:         continue
00709:     found[gid] = (str(patch.get("Title") or ""), patch.get("ImageIcon"), core)
00710: for key, body in sets:
00711:     parts = key.split(":")
00712:     if len(parts) != 3 or parts[2] != user:
00713:         continue
00714:     try:
00715:         data = json.loads(body) or {}
00716:         gid = int(data.get("GameId") or 0)
00717:         core = core_of(set_achievements(data))
00718:     except Exception:
00719:         continue
00720:     if gid > 0 and core and not (gid in found and found[gid][2]):
00721:         found[gid] = (str(data.get("Title") or ""), data.get("ImageIconUrl") or data.get("ImageIcon"), core)
00722: games = []
00723: for gid, (title, icon, core) in found.items():
00724:     if gid <= 0 or not core:
00725:         continue
00726:     points = {int(a["ID"]): int(a.get("Points") or 0) for a in core}
00727:     queued = pending & set(points)
00728:     unlocked = None   # unknown until the store's unlock row is read
00729:     row = unlock_rows.get("unlocks:%d:%s:0" % (gid, user))   # the casual row (cache_keys.unlocks: a trailing 0)
00730:     if row is not None:
00731:         try:
00732:             data = json.loads(row)
00733:             values = data.get("UserUnlocks") if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("Success") is not False else None
00734:             if isinstance(values, list):
00735:                 unlocked = ({int(u) for u in values} | queued) & set(points)
00736:         except Exception:
00737:             unlocked = None
00738:     games.append({"id": gid, "title": title, "icon": icon_url(icon),
00739:                   "achievements": len(points), "points": sum(points.values()),
00740:                   "unlocked": None if unlocked is None else len(unlocked),
00741:                   "unlockedPoints": None if unlocked is None else sum(points[i] for i in unlocked),
00742:                   "pending": len(queued)})
00743: for game in sorted(games, key=lambda g: g["id"]):
00744:     print(json.dumps(game, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False))
00745: PY_SUMMARY
00746:     local RC=$?
00747:     [ "${RC}" -eq 0 ] || cannot_tell "the proxy's store at ${QUEUE} could not be read"
00748: }
00749: 
00750: # The account's points from the proxy's cached sign-in (the login2 row of the
00751: # signed-in user, keyed by the user name in lower case as cache_keys.py
00752: # normalises it). The row carries the session token; the two numbers are
00753: # all that leaves this function.
00754: do_account() {
00755:     if [ "$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "${QUEUE}" ]; then
00756:         return 1
00757:     fi
00758:     local USER LINE
00759:     USER="$(setting "${USER_KEY}")"
00760:     [ -n "${USER}" ] || return 1
00761:     # Exit 1 is "no such row", said apart from a store that cannot be read
00762:     # (exit 3): an account nobody signed in is not the same as a store the
00763:     # page should not trust, and only the second is a cannot_tell.
00764:     LINE="$(python3 -c '
00765: import json, sqlite3, sys
00766: try:
00767:     db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % sys.argv[1], uri=True, timeout=1.0)
00768:     row = db.execute("SELECT responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey = ?", ("login2::" + sys.argv[2].strip().lower(),)).fetchone()
00769: except Exception:
00770:     sys.exit(3)
00771: if row is None:
00772:     sys.exit(1)
00773: try:
00774:     body = json.loads(row[0])
00775: except Exception:
00776:     sys.exit(3)
00777: # The row the proxy writes from a token (auth.cache_token_credentials) has no
00778: # Score: nothing is cached about the points, and an absent number is never
00779: # printed as 0.
00780: if not isinstance(body, dict) or body.get("Score") is None or body.get("SoftcoreScore") is None:
00781:     sys.exit(1)
00782: try:
00783:     score = int(body["Score"])
00784:     softcore = int(body["SoftcoreScore"])
00785: except Exception:
00786:     sys.exit(3)
00787: print("score=%d softcore=%d" % (score, softcore))
00788: ' "${QUEUE}" "${USER}" 2>/dev/null)"
00789:     local RC=$?
00790:     if [ "${RC}" -eq 1 ]; then
00791:         return 1
00792:     elif [ "${RC}" -ne 0 ]; then
00793:         cannot_tell "the proxy's store at ${QUEUE} could not be read"
00794:     fi
00795:     case "${LINE}" in
00796:         score=*\ softcore=*) ;;
00797:         *) cannot_tell "the proxy's store answered '${LINE}', not the account's points" ;;
00798:     esac
00799:     echo "${LINE}"
00800:     return 0
00801: }
00802: 
00803: do_flushed() {
00804:     [ -e "${FLUSH_STAMP}" ] || return 1
00805:     # Taken before it is read: the rename is one step, so a stamp the
00806:     # service replaces after this moment is a new file this call never
00807:     # touches (it is the next caller's), and of two callers only the one
00808:     # whose rename succeeded has anything to report. Whatever was taken is
00809:     # removed before it is judged, so a stamp that says nothing went, or
00810:     # nothing readable, is gone too and never read twice.
00811:     local MINE="${FLUSH_STAMP}.$$" LINE
00812:     mv -f "${FLUSH_STAMP}" "${MINE}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
00813:     LINE="$(head -n 1 "${MINE}" 2>/dev/null)"
00814:     rm -f "${MINE}"
00815:     if [[ "${LINE}" =~ ^[0-9]+\ [1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
00816:         echo "${LINE}"
00817:         return 0
00818:     fi
00819:     return 1
00820: }
00821: 
00822: # ---- the scan -------------------------------------------------------------
00823: 
00824: # The progress file (fork #189): whole or not at all (temp + rename), so a
00825: # reader never sees half a line; RUN_ROUTE is set by the route before its
00826: # first mark. $1 is the rest of the line (" index=<i> total=<n> name=<g>").
00827: mark_running() {
00828:     printf 'route=%s at=%s%s\n' "${RUN_ROUTE:-run}" "$(date +%s)" "${1:-}" > "${RUNNING}.tmp" 2>/dev/null \
00829:         && mv -f "${RUNNING}.tmp" "${RUNNING}" 2>/dev/null
00830: }
00831: unmark_running() { rm -f "${RUNNING}" "${RUNNING}.tmp"; }
00832: 
00833: # A line for the page: ">>> <word> <fields>". Everything else on stdout is
00834: # the client's own output, which the page shows nothing of.
00835: tell() {
00836:     printf '>>> %s\n' "$*"
00837: }
00838: 
00839: # The scan's own log, rotated once past a megabyte. The client's lines are
00840: # file names and reasons; nothing from system.cfg is ever written here.
00841: slog() {
00842:     mkdir -p "${PROXY_DIR}" 2>/dev/null
00843:     if [ -e "${SCAN_LOG}" ] && [ "$(stat -c %s "${SCAN_LOG}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 1048576 ]; then
00844:         mv -f "${SCAN_LOG}" "${SCAN_LOG}.1"
00845:     fi
00846:     printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >> "${SCAN_LOG}"
00847: }
00848: 
00849: # How many games are cached, from the client's export. One id per line, so
00850: # the count is the line count; absent means none yet. Falls back to asking
00851: # the client when the export is missing but a store exists, and to 0 when
00852: # even that cannot be read -- a number that is not known is never invented.
00853: # RetroArch's play history (fork #299): the link's return looks for games
00854: # played since the last attempt and nothing else, so a wake with no game
00855: # played costs nothing and shows nothing. RetroArch 1.22 with
00856: # content_history_directory = "default" writes it under playlist_directory
00857: # as builtin/content_history.lpl, beside the video, music and image
00858: # histories -- not at content_history_path, which the config still names
00859: # and which the RG35XX SP never had (fork #306: the check read "no game
00860: # played" at every link for a day). Both are read from retroarch.cfg (~ is
00861: # /storage) and the newest file wins; a missing file loses to one that
00862: # exists. PPSSPP's ppsspp.ini is read beside them: it is the toggle's other
00863: # emulator (D-RA-002), the recently played pass reads its [Recent] list as
00864: # well as RetroArch's history (the client's load_content_history_paths), and
00865: # the file is written at every PPSSPP launch (cheevos_ppsspp.sh) and exit, so
00866: # a game played in PPSSPP alone is a game played (#308 F-RA-13).
00867: # RAOFFLINEPROXY_HISTORY overrides them all (the scripts suite's fixture).
00868: PPSSPP_INI=/storage/.config/ppsspp/PSP/SYSTEM/ppsspp.ini
00869: history_path() {
00870:     local CFG=/storage/.config/retroarch/retroarch.cfg P D BUILTIN NEWEST=""
00871:     if [ -n "${RAOFFLINEPROXY_HISTORY:-}" ]; then
00872:         printf '%s\n' "${RAOFFLINEPROXY_HISTORY}"
00873:         return 0
00874:     fi
00875:     P="$(sed -n 's/^content_history_path = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "${CFG}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
00876:     case "${P}" in "~/"*) P="/storage/${P#\~/}" ;; esac
00877:     P="${P:-/storage/.config/retroarch/content_history.lpl}"
00878:     D="$(sed -n 's/^playlist_directory = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "${CFG}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
00879:     case "${D}" in "~/"*) D="/storage/${D#\~/}" ;; esac
00880:     BUILTIN="${D:-/storage/playlists}/builtin/content_history.lpl"
00881:     for F in "${BUILTIN}" "${P}" "${PPSSPP_INI}"; do
00882:         [ -e "${F}" ] || continue
00883:         if [ -z "${NEWEST}" ] || [ "${F}" -nt "${NEWEST}" ]; then NEWEST="${F}"; fi
00884:     done
00885:     printf '%s\n' "${NEWEST:-${BUILTIN}}"
00886: }
00887: 
00888: count_ready() {
00889:     local N=""
00890:     if [ -s "${READY_FILE}" ]; then
00891:         N="$(grep -c -E '^[0-9]+$' "${READY_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
00892:     elif [ -e "${QUEUE}" ]; then
00893:         N="$(${PROXY_PY} cached-games-count 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
00894:     fi
00895:     case "${N}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) N=0 ;; esac
00896:     echo "${N}"
00897: }
00898: 
00899: do_ready() {
00900:     count_ready
00901: }

00903: # listening [--wait N] (#308 F-RA-26): the unit was Type=simple, so
00904: # `systemctl start` -- and with it enable, which routes the emulators to
00905: # the proxy once it returns, and the Before= that holds the interface --
00906: # returned the moment Python began importing, seconds before the port was
00907: # bound on a handheld; a launch in that window met a refused connection,
00908: # which makes rcheevos give up achievements for the session. The unit's
00909: # ExecStartPost runs this, bounded, so "started" means "listening". The
00910: # socket table is read, not a tool's output (netstat is not a dependency
00911: # of anything here); 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 on port 8080
00912: # (1F90) in state LISTEN (0A) count -- the listeners that take the IPv4
00913: # connection to 127.0.0.1:8080 the emulators are given. ::1 does not take
00914: # it, and :: may be IPv6-only, which the table does not say, so neither
00915: # counts (audit of the fixes, gpt G-D-02). Leaving :: out turns the proxy
00916: # away never: its sockets are IPv4 -- proxy_service.py's ThreadingTCPServer
00917: # keeps socketserver.TCPServer's AF_INET (patched client, line 267), boot.py
00918: # makes and adopts AF_INET sockets (lines 32 and 58), and nothing here sets
00919: # proxy_host, whose default is 127.0.0.1 (config.py:367) -- and the scripts
00920: # suite runs the pinned client's run-service in a network namespace of its
00921: # own and holds this check to its socket, so a pin that moves to `::` fails
00922: # there first (audit of the fix round, claude G2-D-01, the blind pass's
00923: # S-26, PL-033). RAOFFLINEPROXY_PROC_NET stands in for /proc/net (the
00924: # scripts suite's fixture).
00925: port_listening() {
00926:     local F SL LOCAL REM ST REST
00927:     for F in "${RAOFFLINEPROXY_PROC_NET:-/proc/net}/tcp" "${RAOFFLINEPROXY_PROC_NET:-/proc/net}/tcp6"; do
00928:         [ -r "${F}" ] || continue
00929:         while read -r SL LOCAL REM ST REST; do
00930:             [ "${ST}" = "0A" ] || continue
00931:             case "${LOCAL}" in
00932:                 0100007F:1F90|00000000:1F90|0000000000000000FFFF00000100007F:1F90) return 0 ;;
00933:             esac
00934:         done < "${F}"
00935:     done
00936:     return 1
00937: }
00938: 
00939: do_listening() {
00940:     local TRIES=1 T=0
00941:     if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
00942:         if [ "${1}" != "--wait" ] || [ -z "${2:-}" ] || [ -n "${2//[0-9]/}" ]; then
00943:             echo "usage: raofflineproxy-ctl listening [--wait <seconds>]" >&2
00944:             exit ${EX_USAGE}
00945:         fi
00946:         TRIES="${2}"
00947:     fi
00948:     while :; do
00949:         T=$((T + 1))
00950:         port_listening && return 0
00951:         [ "${T}" -lt "${TRIES}" ] || break
00952:         sleep 1
00953:     done
00954:     say "listening: nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:8080 after ${T} look(s)"
00955:     return 1
00956: }
00957: 
00958: # The games ready for the signed-in account, one id a line into $1: those
00959: # with the account's unlocks row and an achievementsets row of the game --
00960: # the rows a launch reads (RetroArch asks achievementsets, not patch), so a
00961: # game a launch cached is ready before any patch row exists. The walk's
00962: # "already cached" (list_jobs whole_games) is the same rule (audit of the
00963: # fixes, claude G-D-08, gpt G-D-04). A sets row's GameId is read from the
00964: # first 512 characters, where the service writes it, and from the whole body
00965: # only when they do not hold it, so the store's bodies are not parsed whole
00966: # at every run. The head answers only with the body's own key -- not a
00967: # nested set's (Sets[].GameId) -- and a number that ends inside it -- not
00968: # one the cut ends in ("GameId":15 of 153); anything less is the whole
00969: # body's parse, so the two ways of reading a row cannot disagree (audit of
00970: # the fix round, gpt G2-D-01, claude G2-D-08). head_game_id is the same text
00971: # in list_jobs' whole_games. added= is how many ids a run adds to this set
00972: # -- the games that became ready for this player (fork #298's "games new to
00973: # the store"), counted from the store rather than from the run's cache
00974: # operations (#308 F-RA-10, F-RA-15). Exit non-zero when the store cannot
00975: # be read.
00976: ready_games_into() {
00977:     : > "$1" || return 1
00978:     [ -e "${QUEUE}" ] || return 0
00979:     python3 -c '
00980: import json, re, sqlite3, sys
00981: store, user = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2].strip().lower()
00982: db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % store, uri=True, timeout=1.0)
00983: HEAD_VALUE = re.compile(r"\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*[,}]")
00984: HEAD_COLON = re.compile(r"\s*:")
00985: def head_game_id(head):
00986:     depth, i, n = 0, 0, len(head)
00987:     while i < n:
00988:         c = head[i]
00989:         if c == "\"":
00990:             j = i + 1
00991:             while j < n and head[j] != "\"":
00992:                 j += 2 if head[j] == "\\" else 1
00993:             if j >= n:
00994:                 return None
00995:             if depth == 1 and head[i + 1:j] == "GameId":
00996:                 whole = HEAD_VALUE.match(head, j + 1)
00997:                 if whole:
00998:                     return int(whole.group(1))
00999:                 if HEAD_COLON.match(head, j + 1):
01000:                     return None
01001:             i = j + 1
01002:             continue
01003:         if c in "{[":
01004:             depth += 1
01005:         elif c in "}]":
01006:             depth -= 1
01007:         i += 1
01008:     return None
01009: unlocks, sets = set(), set()
01010: for key, head in db.execute("SELECT cacheKey, substr(responseBody, 1, 512) FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey LIKE ? OR cacheKey LIKE ?", ("unlocks:%", "achievementsets:%")).fetchall():
01011:     parts = key.split(":")
01012:     if parts[0] == "unlocks":
01013:         if len(parts) == 4 and parts[2] == user and parts[3] == "0" and parts[1].isdigit():
01014:             unlocks.add(int(parts[1]))
01015:         continue
01016:     if len(parts) != 3 or parts[2] != user:
01017:         continue
01018:     gid = head_game_id(head or "")
01019:     if gid is None:
01020:         try:
01021:             body = db.execute("SELECT responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey = ?", (key,)).fetchone()[0]
01022:             gid = int((json.loads(body) or {}).get("GameId") or 0)
01023:         except Exception:
01024:             gid = 0
01025:     if gid > 0:
01026:         sets.add(gid)
01027: for g in sorted(unlocks & sets):
01028:     print(g)
01029: ' "${QUEUE}" "$(setting "${USER_KEY}")" > "$1" 2>/dev/null
01030: }
01031: 
01032: # How many games a run made ready: the ids in the after file ($2) that the
01033: # before file ($1) does not hold. Prints nothing and fails when either could
01034: # not be read; the caller says so through added_count, and never puts a
01035: # count of its own in this one's place.
01036: games_made_ready() {
01037:     [ -n "${1}" ] && [ -n "${2}" ] && [ -e "${1}" ] && [ -e "${2}" ] || return 1
01038:     local NEWIDS RC N=0
01039:     # grep says 0 when it selected lines, 1 when none, 2 when it could not
01040:     # read: only the first two are an answer. A count taken after the pipe
01041:     # read a failed comparison as 0 new games (audit of the fixes, gpt
01042:     # G-D-05).
01043:     NEWIDS="$(grep -vxF -f "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null)"
01044:     RC=$?
01045:     [ "${RC}" -le 1 ] || return 1
01046:     [ -n "${NEWIDS}" ] && N="$(printf '%s\n' "${NEWIDS}" | grep -c .)"
01047:     echo "${N}"
01048: }
01049: 
01050: # added= as the stamp and the log say it: the measured count ($1) when there
01051: # is one; 0 when the run cached nothing ($2), since a run that cached
01052: # nothing made nothing ready; otherwise the word unknown. Never the run's
01053: # cache operations: they count a second dump of a game already ready, and
01054: # the top-up card says MORE GAMES ARE READY from this number (audit of the
01055: # fix round, gpt G2-D-02, the blind pass's S-24, PL-031). The interface's
01056: # reader (CloudText::parseScanStamp) passes over a value that is not a
01057: # number, as for a stamp that does not say.
01058: added_count() { # <measured count, or empty> <cached>
01059:     if [ -n "${1}" ]; then
01060:         echo "${1}"
01061:     elif [ "${2:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
01062:         echo unknown
01063:     else
01064:         echo 0
01065:     fi
01066: }
01067: 
01068: # "<epoch> <rc> <route> cached=<n> skipped=<m> ready=<total> limit=<0|1>
01069: # indexed=<i> errors=<e> added=<k> [why=<TOKEN>] [note=<TOKEN>]", written whole or not at all (a
01070: # rename), so the page never reads half a line. The page reads the keys it
01071: # knows and passes over the rest (CloudText::parseScanStamp), so indexed=
01072: # and errors= are for the log and for whoever reads the file.
01073: write_stamp() {
01074:     local RC="$1" ROUTE="$2" CACHED="$3" SKIPPED="$4" READY="$5" LIMIT="$6" INDEXED="${7:-0}" ERRORS="${8:-0}" WHY="${9:-}"
01075:     # added (fork #298): the games this run made ready for the account, as
01076:     # measured -- the tenth argument; a run that gives none, or whose
01077:     # measurement failed, is said by added_count, never counted as every
01078:     # game it cached (PL-031).
01079:     local ADDED
01080:     ADDED="$(added_count "${10:-}" "${CACHED}")"
01081:     # truncated=1 (#307 PL-059): the walk over unindexed folders stopped at
01082:     # the cap, and the games past it are the next scan's. Written only when
01083:     # it is 1; CloudText::parseScanStamp reads it.
01084:     local TRUNCATED="${11:-0}"
01085:     # note=NO_GAMES (fork #329): the run completed with nothing to look at;
01086:     # the twelfth argument, written only when given. The page reads it
01087:     # (CloudText::parseScanStamp) for the line under the row.
01088:     local NOTE="${12:-}"
01089:     local LINE="$(date +%s) ${RC} ${ROUTE} cached=${CACHED} skipped=${SKIPPED} ready=${READY} limit=${LIMIT} indexed=${INDEXED} errors=${ERRORS} added=${ADDED}"
01090:     [ "${TRUNCATED}" = "1" ] && LINE="${LINE} truncated=1"
01091:     [ -n "${WHY}" ] && LINE="${LINE} why=${WHY}"
01092:     [ -n "${NOTE}" ] && LINE="${LINE} note=${NOTE}"
01093:     mkdir -p "${PROXY_DIR}" || return 1
01094:     printf '%s\n' "${LINE}" > "${SCAN_STAMP}.tmp" && mv -f "${SCAN_STAMP}.tmp" "${SCAN_STAMP}"
01095: }
01096: 
01097: # The walk's proposed cursor (scan-cursor.next, from list_jobs) becomes the
01098: # cursor: a path to walk on from, or none when the walk came round. Kept
01099: # only after a run that worked through its jobs (audit of the fixes, claude
01100: # G-D-06), and read back once written, since the continuation the page
01101: # promises rests on it (gpt G-D-06). Exit 1 when it could not be kept.
01102: commit_cursor() {
01103:     local WANT
01104:     [ -f "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next" ] || return 1
01105:     WANT="$(cat "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
01106:     if [ -z "${WANT}" ]; then
01107:         rm -f "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next"
01108:         rm -f "${SCAN_CURSOR}" 2>/dev/null
01109:         [ ! -e "${SCAN_CURSOR}" ]
01110:         return
01111:     fi
01112:     [ ! -d "${SCAN_CURSOR}" ] && mv -f "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next" "${SCAN_CURSOR}" 2>/dev/null \
01113:         && [ "$(cat "${SCAN_CURSOR}" 2>/dev/null)" = "${WANT}" ]
01114: }
01115: 
01116: # The account EmulationStation signed in with: a user name and either the
01117: # token it wrote after the sign-in or the password it will sign in with.
01118: # Presence only; the values stay in system.cfg.
01119: have_account() {
01120:     [ -n "$(setting "${USER_KEY}")" ] || return 1
01121:     [ -n "$(setting "${TOKEN_KEY}")" ] || [ -n "$(setting "${PASSWORD_KEY}")" ]
01122: }
01123: 
01124: # The proxy's own answer to "is RetroAchievements reachable": probe-online
01125: # sends one HEAD to retroachievements.org (a fresh process asks every time;
01126: # its thirty-second memory is per process) and writes the answer to
01127: # online_state.json in its config folder, printing nothing. It is pointed
01128: # at a folder of its own for the call: the service's online_state.json is
01129: # the service's (its monitor writes it at start and on a change, and the
01130: # interface reads it as the proxy's own view, D-RA-011), and a probe from
01131: # here that lands in a resolver lag would otherwise write "false" over it
01132: # with nothing to correct it until the service's next transition (#186
01133: # PL-03). Anything but a readable "online": true reads as offline -- a
01134: # check that cannot run has not passed.
01135: is_online() {
01136:     local SCRATCH ANSWER=1
01137:     SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d /tmp/raofflineproxy-probe.XXXXXX)" || return 1
01138:     if RAOFFLINEPROXY_CONFIG_DIR="${SCRATCH}" ${PROXY_PY} probe-online >/dev/null 2>&1; then
01139:         grep -q -E '"online": *true' "${SCRATCH}/online_state.json" 2>/dev/null && ANSWER=0
01140:     fi
01141:     rm -rf "${SCRATCH}"
01142:     return ${ANSWER}
01143: }
01144: 
01145: # Seconds left of a run's deadline, from its START; never negative.
01146: time_left() {
01147:     local L=$(( TOPUP_TIMEOUT - ($(date +%s) - ${1}) ))
01148:     [ "${L}" -gt 0 ] || L=0
01149:     echo "${L}"
01150: }
01151: 
01152: # A sleep that a SIGTERM interrupts: the shell waits on a background sleep,
01153: # and wait returns the moment a trapped signal arrives, so disable is not
01154: # kept waiting for a probe interval to run out.
01155: pause() {
01156:     sleep "${1}" &
01157:     wait $! 2>/dev/null
01158: }
01159: 
01160: # What both verbs refuse before they touch anything, in the order a player
01161: # would fix them: the toggle, then the account. Exit codes only; the page
01162: # says them.
01163: refuse_unless_ready() {
01164:     local VERB="$1"
01165:     if [ "$(as_flag "$(setting "${KEY}")")" != "1" ]; then
01166:         say "${VERB}: refused, offline RetroAchievements is off"
01167:         tell "why TOGGLE_OFF"
01168:         exit ${EX_CONFIG}
01169:     fi
01170:     if ! have_account; then
01171:         say "${VERB}: refused, no RetroAchievements account is signed in"
01172:         tell "why NO_ACCOUNT"
01173:         exit ${EX_NOPERM}
01174:     fi
01175: }
01176: 
01177: # One scan or top-up at a time (the lock is held for the rest of the run;
01178: # the fd closes with the process). Exit 75 when another holds it -- except
01179: # for the top-up that follows the interface's index (topup --after-index),
01180: # which waits its turn for what is left of its deadline ($3, the run's
01181: # START; the wait spends from the same fifteen minutes as the rest, #186
01182: # PL-28): it is the one run that knows the index has just grown, and the
01183: # top-up ahead of it read the index before that. Busybox flock has no -w,
01184: # so the wait is a loop. The file is opened without truncating it, and the
01185: # holder writes its pid on the first line once it has the lock, which is
01186: # how disable finds a run to stop (#186 PL-30) -- a run that finds the lock
01187: # taken has not wiped the holder's pid by opening the file.
01188: take_lock() {
01189:     local VERB="$1" WAIT="${2:-0}" START="${3:-0}"
01190:     exec 9<>"${SCAN_LOCK}" || fail "cannot open ${SCAN_LOCK}"
01191:     until flock -n 9; do
01192:         if [ "${WAIT}" -eq 0 ] || [ "$(time_left "${START}")" -le 10 ]; then
01193:             say "${VERB}: another scan or top-up is running"
01194:             exit ${EX_TEMPFAIL}
01195:         fi
01196:         pause 10
01197:     done
01198:     printf '%s\n' "$$" >&9
01199:     # The lock is held, so no run is live: a progress file still here was a
01200:     # run that died without its EXIT trap (a kill -9, a power cut), and the
01201:     # interface has been ignoring it since its 900 s bound. Removed here, at
01202:     # the one point every verb passes (#189 box 3's "and removed"; the
01203:     # seat's G-08 under audit #258).
01204:     rm -f "${RUNNING}" "${RUNNING}.tmp"
01205: }
01206: 
01207: # The games to cache, one job per line into $1, in the client's own terms
01208: # where it has any, and in the interface's where it has the better ones
01209: # (D-RA-013):
01210: #
01211: #   I<TAB><gameId><TAB><hash><TAB><path>   from the interface's index
01212: #   H<TAB><TAB><TAB><path>                 to be hashed and looked up
01213: #
01214: # The interface's index is what the hasher wrote (INDEX NEW GAMES AT
01215: # STARTUP, INDEX GAMES): per system, the games' <cheevosHash> and
01216: # <cheevosId> in gamelist.xml -- beside the ROMs, else under the interface's
01217: # gamelists/<system>/ -- overlaid with the per-game files under its
01218: # recovery/<system>/, which is where a change lives until the interface
01219: # writes the gamelist at its next clean exit (a recovery file whose
01220: # parentHash is not the current gamelist's size is stale, and skipped as
01221: # the interface skips it). A system has an index when any
01222: # of its games carries a cheevosHash: the hasher writes the hash for every
01223: # game it looked at and the id only for the ones RetroAchievements knows, so
01224: # a system whose games all came back without a set is indexed too, and
01225: # nothing in it is hashed again. In an indexed system the jobs are the games
01226: # with a cheevosId whose file is still there and whose id the client has not
01227: # cached (its own export of cached ids, the count `ready` reads); the rest
01228: # of the system -- games with no set, and games added since the index ran --
01229: # is left to the index. A system with no index at all keeps today's walk
01230: # (mode all): every ROM under its folder, in the client's own terms -- its
01231: # extension list decides what is a ROM (is_supported_browser_file, archives
01232: # included), its cached-path record what is already done, its history reader
01233: # what was played (most recent first, then newest file first) -- less hidden
01234: # files and folders, the scraper's folders, empty files, and a .bin beside a
01235: # .cue, .gdi or .m3u. Mode indexed writes the I jobs alone: the top-up on
01236: # connect never hashes a library nobody asked it to.
01237: #
01238: # "Already cached" is asked of the signed-in account's rows and this hash's
01239: # (#186 PL-23): the proxy serves a launch from patch:<id>:<user>,
01240: # unlocks:<id>:<user>:0 and achievementsets:<hash>:<user>, so a game is
01241: # cached when all three are there for this account and this dump, and a
01242: # job again when any is missing -- a fetch that failed after the first row
01243: # was written, a set the client's eviction took at sixty days (#186 PL-02),
01244: # a second account on the device, a second dump of a game. The account
01245: # name reaches the listing through the environment (RA_SCAN_USER), never a
01246: # command line. The walk's "already done" stays the client's own record
01247: # (the ROM's path on this account's patch rows).
01248: #
01249: # The systems and their folders come from the interface's own files, read
01250: # as it reads them: the base es_systems.cfg (custom, user or image copy) and
01251: # the es_systems_*.cfg merged into it (#308 F-RA-06); the walk's
01252: # folders from SCAN_SYSTEMS as before, less any folder an indexed system
01253: # owns. The walk stops at the client's cap of files (MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES),
01254: # counted over the files not yet cached and begun from the cursor the last
01255: # cut walk left (scan-cursor, $6), so the cap bounds one run's work and never
01256: # the library: a second run walks past what the first cached (#186 PL-17)
01257: # and past what the first could not cache (#307 PL-059). $3 bounds the
01258: # listing in seconds (0: no bound). Prints
01259: # "found=<seen> new=<jobs> cached=<seen-jobs> indexed=<I> hashing=<H>
01260: # truncated=<0|1>" on stdout.
01261: list_jobs() {
01262:     local BUDGET="${3:-0}"
01263:     local -a BOUND=()
01264:     [ "${BUDGET}" -gt 0 ] && BOUND=(timeout "${BUDGET}")
01265:     RA_SCAN_USER="$(setting "${USER_KEY}")" "${BOUND[@]}" python3 - "$1" "${2:-all}" "${ROMS_ROOT}" "${ES_DIR}" "${SCAN_SYSTEMS}" "${SCAN_CURSOR}" <<'PY'
01266: import json, os, re, sqlite3, sys
01267: import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
01268: from pathlib import Path
01269: from raofflineproxy import cache_keys
01270: from raofflineproxy.config import DATABASE_FILE, load_config
01271: from raofflineproxy.rom_browser import (
01272:     MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES, is_supported_browser_file, normalize_cached_rom_path,
01273: )
01274: from raofflineproxy.smart_cache import load_content_history_paths
01275: from raofflineproxy.storage import Storage
01276: 
01277: out, mode, roms_root, es_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], Path(sys.argv[3]), Path(sys.argv[4])
01278: walk_systems = sys.argv[5].split()
01279: cursor_file = Path(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 and sys.argv[6] else None
01280: user = cache_keys.normalize_user(os.environ.get("RA_SCAN_USER", ""))
01281: SKIP_DIRS = {
01282:     "images", "videos", "manuals", "media", "downloaded_images", "downloaded_videos",
01283:     "downloaded_manuals", "imgs", "savestates", "screenshots", "saves", "savefiles",
01284: }
01285: DISC_SHEETS = (".cue", ".gdi", ".m3u")
01286: 
01287: 
01288: def es_systems():
01289:     """(name, folder) per <system>, read as the interface reads them (#308
01290:     F-RA-06): SystemData::getConfigPath takes the first of the user's
01291:     es_systems_custom.cfg, the user's es_systems.cfg, the one beside the
01292:     binary and the image's as the base -- a custom file is the whole base
01293:     there too -- and loadAdditionnalConfig then merges every es_systems_*.cfg
01294:     in the user's folder and beside the binary into it by name: a known
01295:     system's tags replaced (a tag with no text dropped, <emulators> kept), a
01296:     new one appended, and a file that does not parse ends the merging, as it
01297:     does there."""
01298:     root = None
01299:     for cfg in (es_dir / "es_systems_custom.cfg", es_dir / "es_systems.cfg",
01300:                 Path("/usr/bin/es_systems.cfg"), Path("/etc/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg"),
01301:                 Path("/usr/config/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg")):
01302:         if not cfg.is_file():
01303:             continue
01304:         try:
01305:             root = ET.parse(cfg).getroot()
01306:         except Exception:
01307:             continue
01308:         break
01309:     if root is None:
01310:         return []
01311:     order, tags = [], {}
01312:     for system in root.iter("system"):
01313:         name = (system.findtext("name") or "").strip()
01314:         if name and name not in tags:
01315:             order.append(name)
01316:             tags[name] = {child.tag: child.text or "" for child in system}
01317:     merging = True
01318:     for folder in dict.fromkeys((es_dir, Path("/usr/bin"))):
01319:         if not merging:
01320:             break
01321:         try:
01322:             extras = sorted(e for e in folder.iterdir() if e.name.startswith("es_systems_") and e.suffix == ".cfg")
01323:         except OSError:
01324:             continue
01325:         for extra in extras:
01326:             try:
01327:                 extra_root = ET.parse(extra).getroot()
01328:             except Exception:
01329:                 merging = False
01330:                 break
01331:             if extra_root.tag != "systemList":
01332:                 merging = False
01333:                 break
01334:             for system in extra_root.findall("system"):
01335:                 name = (system.findtext("name") or "").strip()
01336:                 if not name:
01337:                     continue
01338:                 if name not in tags:
01339:                     order.append(name)
01340:                     tags[name] = {child.tag: child.text or "" for child in system}
01341:                     continue
01342:                 for child in system:
01343:                     if child.tag == "name":
01344:                         continue
01345:                     tags[name].pop(child.tag, None)
01346:                     if child.tag == "emulators" or (child.text or ""):
01347:                         tags[name][child.tag] = child.text or ""
01348:     found = []
01349:     for name in order:
01350:         folder = (tags[name].get("path") or "").strip()
01351:         if folder:
01352:             found.append((name, Path(os.path.expanduser(folder))))
01353:     return found
01354: 
01355: 
01356: def game_path(folder, text):
01357:     text = text.strip()
01358:     if text.startswith("./"):
01359:         return folder / text[2:]
01360:     if text.startswith("/"):
01361:         return Path(text)
01362:     return folder / text
01363: 
01364: 
01365: def read_index(name, folder):
01366:     """{path: (cheevosHash, cheevosId)} for one system, read as the
01367:     interface reads it (Gamelist.cpp parseGamelist): gamelist.xml, then the
01368:     recovery files over it. A recovery file is a game's whole metadata as the
01369:     interface last had it, so its values replace the gamelist's -- but only
01370:     while its parentHash names the gamelist it was written beside (the
01371:     gamelist's size in bytes, 0 when there is none); one that names another
01372:     is stale and skipped, as the interface skips it."""
01373:     entries = {}
01374: 
01375:     def take(doc, parent=None):
01376:         try:
01377:             root = ET.parse(doc).getroot()
01378:         except Exception:
01379:             return
01380:         if parent is not None:
01381:             try:
01382:                 written_beside = int(root.get("parentHash", "0"))
01383:             except ValueError:
01384:                 return
01385:             if written_beside != parent:
01386:                 return
01387:         for game in root.iter("game"):
01388:             text = game.findtext("path") or ""
01389:             if not text.strip():
01390:                 continue
01391:             entries[game_path(folder, text)] = (
01392:                 (game.findtext("cheevosHash") or "").strip(),
01393:                 (game.findtext("cheevosId") or "").strip(),
01394:             )
01395: 
01396:     gamelist = folder / "gamelist.xml"
01397:     if not gamelist.is_file():
01398:         gamelist = es_dir / "gamelists" / name / "gamelist.xml"
01399:     size = 0
01400:     if gamelist.is_file():
01401:         try:
01402:             size = gamelist.stat().st_size
01403:         except OSError:
01404:             size = 0
01405:         take(gamelist)
01406:     recovery = es_dir / "recovery" / name
01407:     if recovery.is_dir():
01408:         for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(recovery):
01409:             dirnames.sort()
01410:             for fn in sorted(filenames):
01411:                 if fn.lower().endswith(".xml"):
01412:                     take(Path(dirpath) / fn, parent=size)

01420: def is_cached(game_id, hash_value):
01421:     """Everything a launch reads, for this account and this dump."""
01422:     return (
01423:         storage.get_cache(cache_keys.patch(game_id, user)) is not None
01424:         and storage.get_cache(cache_keys.unlocks(game_id, user)) is not None
01425:         and storage.get_cache(cache_keys.achievementsets(hash_value, user)) is not None
01426:     )
