```text
01428: 
01429: # The ROMs this account's patch rows name (rom_browser.load_cached_rom_paths,
01430: # narrowed to the account), in the client's own two-component form -- where
01431: # the game is ready for this account (whole_games: its unlocks row and an
01432: # achievementsets row of the game), as is_cached asks of an indexed game. A patch row alone (a fetch that failed after the first write, or
01433: # rows an older client's eviction thinned) used to pass the ROM over for
01434: # ever; now it is a job again (#308 F-RA-14). The dump's own sets row cannot
01435: # be asked here -- an unindexed ROM's hash is what the job finds out.
01436: HEAD_VALUE = re.compile(r"\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*[,}]")
01437: HEAD_COLON = re.compile(r"\s*:")
01438: def head_game_id(head):
01439:     depth, i, n = 0, 0, len(head)
01440:     while i < n:
01441:         c = head[i]
01442:         if c == "\"":
01443:             j = i + 1
01444:             while j < n and head[j] != "\"":
01445:                 j += 2 if head[j] == "\\" else 1
01446:             if j >= n:
01447:                 return None
01448:             if depth == 1 and head[i + 1:j] == "GameId":
01449:                 whole = HEAD_VALUE.match(head, j + 1)
01450:                 if whole:
01451:                     return int(whole.group(1))
01452:                 if HEAD_COLON.match(head, j + 1):
01453:                     return None
01454:             i = j + 1
01455:             continue
01456:         if c in "{[":
01457:             depth += 1
01458:         elif c in "}]":
01459:             depth -= 1
01460:         i += 1
01461:     return None
01462:

01464: def whole_games():
01465:     """The games ready for this account -- the unlocks row and an
01466:     achievementsets row of the game, the rows a launch reads -- by the same
01467:     rule as the shell's ready_games_into (audit of the fixes, claude G-D-08,
01468:     gpt G-D-04). A sets row's GameId is read from its first 512 characters,
01469:     where the service writes it, and from the whole body only when they do
01470:     not hold it: every body parsed whole at every listing was tens of
01471:     megabytes on a large store. The head answers only with the body's own
01472:     key and a number that ends inside it (head_game_id above, the same text
01473:     as in the shell's ready_games_into; audit of the fix round, gpt
01474:     G2-D-01, claude G2-D-08)."""
01475:     unlocks, sets = set(), set()
01476:     try:
01477:         db = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % DATABASE_FILE, uri=True, timeout=1.0)
01478:         rows = db.execute("SELECT cacheKey, substr(responseBody, 1, 512) FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey LIKE ? OR cacheKey LIKE ?", ("unlocks:%", "achievementsets:%")).fetchall()
01479:     except Exception:
01480:         db = None
01481:         rows = ((e.get("cacheKey") or "", e.get("responseBody") or "") for prefix in (cache_keys.PREFIX_UNLOCKS, cache_keys.PREFIX_ACHIEVEMENTSETS) for e in storage.iter_cache_by_prefix(prefix))
01482:     for key, head in rows:
01483:         parts = str(key).split(":")
01484:         if parts[0] == "unlocks":
01485:             if len(parts) == 4 and parts[2] == user and parts[3] == "0" and parts[1].isdigit():
01486:                 unlocks.add(int(parts[1]))
01487:             continue
01488:         if len(parts) != 3 or parts[2] != user:
01489:             continue
01490:         gid = head_game_id((head or "")[:512])
01491:         if gid is None:
01492:             try:
01493:                 body = db.execute("SELECT responseBody FROM api_cache WHERE cacheKey = ?", (key,)).fetchone()[0] if db is not None else head
01494:                 gid = int((json.loads(body) or {}).get("GameId") or 0)
01495:             except Exception:
01496:                 gid = 0
01497:         if gid > 0:
01498:             sets.add(gid)
01499:     if db is not None:
01500:         db.close()
01501:     return unlocks & sets
01502:

01504: whole = whole_games()

01506:     normalize_cached_rom_path(entry["sourceRomPath"])
01507:     for entry in storage.cache_summaries_by_prefix(cache_keys.PREFIX_PATCH)
01508:     if isinstance(entry.get("sourceRomPath"), str) and entry["sourceRomPath"].strip()
01509:     and entry["cacheKey"].endswith(":" + user)
01510:     and cache_keys.parse_game_id_from_patch_key(entry["cacheKey"]) in whole

01518: def mtime(p):

01522:         return 0.0

01525: def by_history(paths):
01526:     """The played ones first, most recent first; then the rest, newest first."""
01527:     order = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(history)}
01528:     played = sorted((p for p in paths if str(p) in order), key=lambda p: order[str(p)])
01529:     rest = sorted((p for p in paths if str(p) not in order), key=mtime, reverse=True)
01530:     return played + rest

01533: indexed_dirs = set()
01534: indexed_seen = 0
01535: indexed_jobs = {}
01536: for name, folder in es_systems():

01538:         continue
01539:     index = read_index(name, folder)
01540:     if not any(h for h, _ in index.values()):
01541:         continue
01542:     try:
01543:         indexed_dirs.add(folder.resolve())
01544:     except OSError:
01545:         indexed_dirs.add(folder)
01546:     for path, (hash_value, id_text) in index.items():
01547:         try:
01548:             game_id = int(id_text)
01549:         except ValueError:
01550:             game_id = 0
01551:         if game_id <= 0 or not hash_value or not path.is_file():
01552:             continue
01553:         indexed_seen += 1
01554:         if path in indexed_jobs or is_cached(game_id, hash_value):
01555:             continue
01556:         indexed_jobs[path] = (game_id, hash_value)
01557: storage.close()

01559: def read_cursor():
01560:     try:
01561:         return cursor_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape").rstrip("\n") if cursor_file else ""
01562:     except OSError:
01563:         return ""
01564: 
01565: 
01566: def propose_cursor(value):
01567:     """The cursor this walk proposes -- the path of the last file it took,
01568:     or nothing when the walk came round -- written whole to
01569:     scan-cursor.next for the ctl to keep once the run has worked through its
01570:     jobs (commit_cursor): a run cancelled or stopped after its listing
01571:     leaves the cursor where it was, so the next scan takes the same slice
01572:     (audit of the fixes, claude G-D-06). False when it could not be written
01573:     -- and the ctl says so rather than promising a continuation it cannot
01574:     keep (gpt G-D-06)."""
01575:     if cursor_file is None:
01576:         return True
01577:     proposal = cursor_file.with_name(cursor_file.name + ".next")
01578:     tmp = proposal.with_name(proposal.name + ".tmp")
01579:     try:
01580:         tmp.write_text(value + "\n" if value else "", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
01581:         os.replace(tmp, proposal)
01582:         return True
01583:     except OSError:
01584:         try:
01585:             tmp.unlink()
01586:         except OSError:
01587:             pass
01588:         return False
01589: 
01590: 
01591: # The walk is a circle from a cursor (#307 PL-059). Cached files are passed
01592: # over before the cap counts (#186 PL-17), but a file that never caches -- a
01593: # ROM RetroAchievements does not know is skipped, and stays uncached --
01594: # counted every run, so the first MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES such files held the front
01595: # of the walk for ever and the files past them were never reached. So a walk
01596: # the cap cuts proposes the path of the last file it took (scan-cursor.next),
01597: # the ctl keeps it as scan-cursor once the run has worked through its jobs,
01598: # and the next walk takes the files after it first, then comes round to the
01599: # start. A walk that fits under the cap removes the cursor; a cursor that
01600: # names a file the walk no longer meets (deleted, or its folder now indexed)
01601: # starts the circle from the top.
01602: walked = []
01603: walked_cached = 0
01604: truncated = 0
01605: cursor_saved = 1
01606: if mode == "all":
01607:     cursor = read_cursor()
01608:     passed = not cursor
01609:     before, after = [], []   # the candidates up to the cursor, and past it
01610:     full = False
01611:     for name in walk_systems:
01612:         root = roms_root / name
01613:         if not root.is_dir():
01614:             continue
01615:         try:
01616:             if root.resolve() in indexed_dirs:
01617:                 continue
01618:         except OSError:
01619:             pass
01620:         for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
01621:             dirnames[:] = sorted(d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith(".") and d.lower() not in SKIP_DIRS)
01622:             has_sheet = any(f.lower().endswith(DISC_SHEETS) for f in filenames)
01623:             for fn in sorted(filenames):
01624:                 if fn.startswith("."):
01625:                     continue
01626:                 path = Path(dirpath) / fn
01627:                 at_cursor = not passed and str(path) == cursor
01628:                 # Before the cursor only the first cap's worth is ever
01629:                 # taken (the circle's tail), so past that the walk only
01630:                 # looks for the cursor.
01631:                 if not passed and len(before) > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES:
01632:                     passed = passed or at_cursor
01633:                     continue
01634:                 take = False
01635:                 if is_supported_browser_file(path) and not (has_sheet and fn.lower().endswith(".bin")):
01636:                     try:
01637:                         take = path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size > 0
01638:                     except OSError:
01639:                         take = False
01640:                 if take and normalize_cached_rom_path(path) in cached_paths:
01641:                     walked_cached += 1
01642:                     take = False
01643:                 if take:
01644:                     (after if passed else before).append(path)
01645:                 passed = passed or at_cursor
01646:                 if len(after) > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES:
01647:                     full = True
01648:                     break
01649:             if full:
01650:                 break
01651:         if full:
01652:             break
01653:     candidates = after + before
01654:     walked = candidates[:MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES]
01655:     truncated = 1 if len(candidates) > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES else 0
01656:     cursor_saved = 1 if propose_cursor(str(walked[-1]) if truncated and walked else "") else 0
01657: 
01658: hash_jobs = walked
01659: 
01660: lines = [f"I\t{indexed_jobs[p][0]}\t{indexed_jobs[p][1]}\t{p}\n" for p in by_history(list(indexed_jobs))]
01661: lines += [f"H\t\t\t{p}\n" for p in by_history(hash_jobs)]
01662: out.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
01663: found = indexed_seen + len(walked) + walked_cached
01664: new = len(lines)
01665: print(f"found={found} new={new} cached={found - new} indexed={len(indexed_jobs)} hashing={len(hash_jobs)} truncated={truncated} cursor_saved={cursor_saved}")
01666: PY
01667: }

01669: # One field of list_jobs' summary line, or 0.
01670: count_of() {
01671:     local V="${1#*${2}=}"
01672:     V="${V%% *}"
01673:     case "${V}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 0 ;; *) echo "${V}" ;; esac
01674: }
01675: 
01676: # The helper that works the job list: beside this script, so a copy of the
01677: # two files runs from anywhere they are put together.
01678: case "$0" in
01679:     */*) HELPER="${0%/*}/raofflineproxy-cache-indexed"; IMAGE_HELPER="${0%/*}/raofflineproxy-cache-images"; REFRESH_HELPER="${0%/*}/raofflineproxy-refresh" ;;
01680:     *)   HELPER="/usr/bin/raofflineproxy-cache-indexed"; IMAGE_HELPER="/usr/bin/raofflineproxy-cache-images"; REFRESH_HELPER="/usr/bin/raofflineproxy-refresh" ;;
01681: esac
01682: 
01683: # Run the job list $2 of $3 games through the helper and read its lines as
01684: # they come -- "OK i/n <file>", "FAIL i/n <file>: <reason>", "DONE cached=
01685: # failed= indexed=" -- stopping it after three lookups in a row that
01686: # RetroAchievements did not answer, or on a refused sign-in, or when the
01687: # client reports its cap. $1 is page (the >>> lines for GuiOfflineScan) or
01688: # quiet (nothing on stdout, for the top-up); $4 a bound in seconds, 0 for
01689: # none. Leaves R_CACHED R_SKIPPED R_ERRORS R_LIMIT R_WHY R_STOPPED R_INDEXED
01690: # R_CLIENT_RC for the caller, and the helper's stderr in the scan log. The
01691: # helper's stdout goes through a fifo so it can be stopped between two lines.
01692: run_jobs() {
01693:     local MODE="$1" LIST="$2" TOTAL="$3" BUDGET="${4:-0}"
01694:     local -a PATHS
01695:     mapfile -t PATHS < "${LIST}"
01696:     JOBS_FIFO="$(mktemp -u /tmp/raofflineproxy-scan-out.XXXXXX)"
01697:     mkfifo "${JOBS_FIFO}" || fail "cannot create ${JOBS_FIFO}"
01698:     if [ "${BUDGET}" -gt 0 ]; then
01699:         timeout "${BUDGET}" python3 "${HELPER}" "${LIST}" > "${JOBS_FIFO}" 2>>"${SCAN_LOG}" &
01700:     else
01701:         python3 "${HELPER}" "${LIST}" > "${JOBS_FIFO}" 2>>"${SCAN_LOG}" &
01702:     fi
01703:     CLIENT=$!
01704:     exec 8< "${JOBS_FIFO}"
01705: 
01706:     R_CACHED=0; R_SKIPPED=0; R_ERRORS=0; R_LIMIT=0; R_WHY=""; R_STOPPED=0; R_INDEXED=0; R_DONE=0
01707:     local IN_A_ROW=0 line index name
01708:     if [ "${TOTAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
01709:         name="${PATHS[0]##*/}"
01710:         mark_running " index=1 total=${TOTAL} name=${name//[[:space:]]/_}"
01711:         [ "${MODE}" = page ] && tell "game 1|${TOTAL}|${name%.*}"
01712:     fi
01713:     while IFS= read -r line <&8; do
01714:         slog "client: ${line}"
01715:         case "${line}" in
01716:             OK\ *)
01717:                 R_CACHED=$((R_CACHED + 1)); IN_A_ROW=0 ;;
01718:             DONE\ *)
01719:                 # The helper's verdict on the games: whatever the process does
01720:                 # afterwards (badge downloads outliving the bound, fork #188) is
01721:                 # not the run's outcome.
01722:                 R_INDEXED="$(count_of "${line}" indexed)"; R_DONE=1
01723:                 continue ;;
01724:             *"Cache limit reached"*)
01725:                 # The client says it will cache no more (no ROCKNIX client
01726:                 # does since patch 004; kept for one that says so): every
01727:                 # further ROM would be hashed and looked up only to be
01728:                 # refused.
01729:                 R_LIMIT=1; R_STOPPED=1
01730:                 slog "run: the client reports its cache limit; stopping"
01731:                 kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null
01732:                 break ;;
01733:             *"No RetroAchievements match"*|*"Hash failed"*|*": not found")
01734:                 # Not a game RetroAchievements knows, or not a file it can
01735:                 # read: the proxy's docs skip these silently, and so does
01736:                 # the page -- counted here for the log and the stamp.
01737:                 R_SKIPPED=$((R_SKIPPED + 1)); IN_A_ROW=0 ;;
01738:             *"login required"*|*"HTTP Error 401"*|*"HTTP Error 403"*)
01739:                 # The account, not the link: no retry changes it.
01740:                 R_WHY=SIGN_IN_REFUSED; R_STOPPED=1
01741:                 kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null
01742:                 break ;;
01743:             FAIL\ *)
01744:                 # A lookup or a fetch that did not come back: the link, the
01745:                 # server, a 429. A run of them is the scan asking a question
01746:                 # nobody is answering.
01747:                 R_ERRORS=$((R_ERRORS + 1)); IN_A_ROW=$((IN_A_ROW + 1))
01748:                 if [ "${IN_A_ROW}" -ge "${ERRORS_IN_A_ROW}" ]; then
01749:                     R_WHY=RETROACHIEVEMENTS_STOPPED_ANSWERING; R_STOPPED=1
01750:                     kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null
01751:                     break
01752:                 fi ;;
01753:             *)
01754:                 continue ;;
01755:         esac
01756:         # The helper finished game i (1-based); what it is on now is i+1.
01757:         index="${line#* }"; index="${index%%/*}"
01758:         case "${index}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) index=0 ;; esac
01759:         if [ "${index}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${index}" -lt "${TOTAL}" ]; then
01760:             name="${PATHS[${index}]##*/}"
01761:             mark_running " index=$((index + 1)) total=${TOTAL} name=${name//[[:space:]]/_}"
01762:         fi
01763:         [ "${MODE}" = page ] || continue
01764:         tell "cached ${R_CACHED}|${R_SKIPPED}"
01765:         if [ "${index}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${index}" -lt "${TOTAL}" ]; then
01766:             tell "game $((index + 1))|${TOTAL}|${name%.*}"
01767:         fi
01768:     done
01769:     exec 8<&-
01770:     wait "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null
01771:     R_CLIENT_RC=$?
01772:     unset CLIENT
01773:     rm -f "${JOBS_FIFO}"; JOBS_FIFO=""
01774:     unmark_running
01775:     if [ "${R_DONE}" -eq 1 ] && [ "${R_CLIENT_RC}" -ne 0 ]; then
01776:         slog "run: the helper had reported DONE and ended with rc ${R_CLIENT_RC} afterwards (badge downloads cut short) -- not the run's verdict (#188)"
01777:     fi
01778: }
01779: 
01780: # A run asked to stop (disable's SIGTERM, #186 PL-30) exits through its
01781: # EXIT trap: the helper is ended, the run's files go, no stamp is written --
01782: # the line under the row keeps the last run that finished.
01783: stopped() {
01784:     say "${1}: stopped; offline RetroAchievements was turned off"
01785:     exit 143
01786: }
01787: 
01788: # A scan the player cancelled from its page (SIGINT from the interface,
01789: # fork #241, D-UI-078). Not a failure: what the run saved stays saved, and
01790: # the next scan passes over those games. So the stamp is written with the
01791: # counts the run had reached -- the line under the row says SKIPPED and the
01792: # ready count is right -- the page is told why, and the run exits 130
01793: # through its EXIT trap (the helper ended, the run's files gone). R_CACHED
01794: # and the rest are the run's so far; before run_jobs they are unset, and
01795: # read as 0. added= is measured as the run's own end measures it -- the
01796: # ready set the run took before its jobs against the store now -- and is
01797: # unknown when either cannot be read, never the games cached so far
01798: # (PL-031).
01799: cancelled() {
01800:     local READY MADE=""
01801:     READY="$(count_ready)"
01802:     if [ -n "${READY_BEFORE:-}" ] && READY_AFTER="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-ready.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null)" && ready_games_into "${READY_AFTER}"; then
01803:         MADE="$(games_made_ready "${READY_BEFORE}" "${READY_AFTER}")"
01804:     fi
01805:     tell "why CANCELLED"
01806:     write_stamp 130 "${1}" "${R_CACHED:-0}" "${R_SKIPPED:-0}" "${READY}" 0 "${R_INDEXED:-0}" "${R_ERRORS:-0}" CANCELLED "${MADE}"
01807:     slog "${1} cancelled by the player: cached=${R_CACHED:-0} skipped=${R_SKIPPED:-0} errors=${R_ERRORS:-0} ready=${READY}"
01808:     say "${1}: cancelled"
01809:     exit 130
01810: }
01811: 
01812: # The images of what is cached, fetched until none is missing (#212). A
01813: # game's achievements and its images are one action to a player -- the
01814: # maintainer, 2026-09-18: "whenever we cache the achievements, we cache the
01815: # images for the achievements" -- so this runs at the end of a scan and of a
01816: # top-up that cached anything, and on its own as the `images` verb.
01817: #
01818: # The helper walks the store, not the library: every cached set row, every
01819: # image path in it, and the ones with no file get fetched. Idempotent (the
01820: # check is the file's existence and the client's own download no-ops on one)
01821: # and resumable (nothing marks a game done but its files), so a run that
01822: # stops at its ceiling costs the next one nothing. Bounded by what is left of
01823: # the caller's deadline, or IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS on its own.
01824: #
01825: # Its verdict is part of the run's (#307 PL-060). A game whose badges are
01826: # missing offline reads as half working (D-RA-027), and a run whose parts
01827: # disagree is COULDN'T FINISH (D-UI-030), so a pass that left images behind
01828: # -- the helper's `why` line, or an exit it gives no reason for -- leaves
01829: # R_IMAGES_WHY=SOME_IMAGES_NOT_SAVED for the caller to stamp, the games
01830: # still counted as cached. A verify slice that did not come round the store
01831: # (the helper's exit 3) is the sweep doing its work a slice a run, by design
01832: # (D-RA-024), and is no failure; every other exit is, a crash included. An
01833: # image the image server does not have (404, 410) is recorded absent by the
01834: # helper and is no failure either: SOME_IMAGES_NOT_SAVED means images that
01835: # did not come this time -- a timeout, a 5xx, a short read -- and are asked
01836: # for again (PL-060's follow-up).
01837: IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS="${RAOFFLINEPROXY_IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS:-300}"
01838: 
01839: run_image_pass() {
01840:     local VERB="$1" SECONDS_LEFT="${2:-${IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS}}" MODE="${3:-}" RC=0
01841:     R_IMAGES_WHY=""
01842:     [ -x "${IMAGE_HELPER}" ] || { slog "${VERB}: no image helper at ${IMAGE_HELPER}"; return 0; }
01843:     # No time left is no pass: the images were not looked at, and the run
01844:     # does not say it finished (audit of the fixes, gpt G-D-01).
01845:     [ "${SECONDS_LEFT}" -gt 10 ] 2>/dev/null || { slog "${VERB}: no time left for the image pass (${SECONDS_LEFT}s); not run"; R_IMAGES_WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG; return 0; }
01846:     slog "${VERB}: image pass, up to ${SECONDS_LEFT}s${MODE:+ (${MODE})}"
01847:     # In the background and waited for, as the jobs and the recently played
01848:     # pass are: bash runs a trap only once the foreground command has
01849:     # returned, so with the helper in the foreground the page's CANCEL (INT)
01850:     # and a stop from disable or STOP IT AND PLAY (TERM) waited for the whole
01851:     # pass before the run could answer either (#307 PL-013, #308 F-RA-11).
01852:     # wait returns the moment a trapped signal arrives, and CLIENT is what
01853:     # the EXIT trap ends. CLIENT is timeout, which puts itself and the
01854:     # helper in a process group of their own: the interface's SIGINT to the
01855:     # run's group reaches this script, not the helper, and the EXIT trap's
01856:     # kill of timeout is forwarded to the helper as SIGTERM -- the path the
01857:     # harness's D23 runs under GNU timeout (audit of the fixes, claude
01858:     # G-D-03).
01859:     # Bounded at the process as well (#308 F-RA-10): the helper checks its
01860:     # --seconds between one blocking call and the next, so it is given ten
01861:     # seconds less than the pass has and timeout ends it at the pass's
01862:     # bound whatever it is blocked on (a timeout is images not saved).
01863:     # shellcheck disable=SC2086 -- MODE is one flag or empty, on purpose
01864:     timeout "${SECONDS_LEFT}" "${IMAGE_HELPER}" --seconds "$(( SECONDS_LEFT - 10 ))" ${MODE} >>"${SCAN_LOG}" 2>&1 &
01865:     CLIENT=$!
01866:     wait "${CLIENT}" || RC=$?
01867:     unset CLIENT
01868:     # 0: every image there. 3: every image there, a verify slice left for
01869:     # the next pass. Anything else -- images left behind (1), no store or
01870:     # account (2), a helper that died -- is the pass not done.
01871:     case "${RC}" in
01872:         0|3) ;;
01873:         *) R_IMAGES_WHY=SOME_IMAGES_NOT_SAVED ;;
01874:     esac
01875:     slog "${VERB}: image pass rc=${RC}${R_IMAGES_WHY:+ why=${R_IMAGES_WHY}}"
01876:     return "${RC}"
01877: }
01878: 
01879: do_images() {
01880:     local MODE=""
01881:     [ "${1:-}" = "--verify" ] && MODE=--verify
01882:     refuse_unless_ready images
01883:     if ! is_online; then
01884:         say "images: refused, this device is offline"
01885:         tell "why NO_NETWORK"
01886:         exit ${EX_UNAVAILABLE}
01887:     fi
01888:     # The lock carries this pid, so `disable` can ask the run to stop
01889:     # (stop_running_run, #186 PL-30); the TERM trap ends the helper and
01890:     # the EXIT trap clears the progress file, as scan's do. The progress
01891:     # line is route=images at=<epoch>: RUN_ROUTE names the verb, and
01892:     # mark_running's argument is the rest of the line, not the verb --
01893:     # `mark_running images` wrote at=<epoch>images (audit #258 PL-013).
01894:     trap 'stopped images' TERM
01895:     RUN_ROUTE=images
01896:     take_lock images
01897:     mark_running
01898:     trap 'unmark_running; [ -n "${CLIENT:-}" ] && kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
01899:     local RC=0
01900:     # Bounded at the process too, a grace past the helper's own --seconds
01901:     # (#308 F-RA-10).
01902:     # shellcheck disable=SC2086 -- MODE is one flag or empty, on purpose
01903:     timeout "$(( IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS + 10 ))" "${IMAGE_HELPER}" --seconds "${IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS}" ${MODE} &
01904:     CLIENT=$!
01905:     wait "${CLIENT}" || RC=$?
01906:     CLIENT=""
01907:     slog "images: rc=${RC}${MODE:+ (${MODE})}"
01908:     exit "${RC}"
01909: }
01910: 
01911: # refresh [--game <id>|--all]. The service's own pass re-reads, each online
01912: # hour while the proxy is idle, the cached games played in the last seven
01913: # days (upstream 59b167c, D-RA-029; patch 005 keeps only its exception
01914: # boundary), which covers the ordinary case -- not every cached game, and not
01915: # daily, as this said until #308 F-RA-28. This is for the player standing in
01916: # front of the device who has just changed
01917: # something on the site -- reset an achievement, earned one elsewhere -- and
01918: # wants it true here before going offline (#223).
01919: do_refresh() {
01920:     local WHICH=()
01921:     case "${1:-}" in
01922:         --all)  WHICH=(--all) ;;
01923:         --game) [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: raofflineproxy-ctl refresh [--all|--game <id>]" >&2; exit ${EX_USAGE}; }
01924:                 WHICH=(--game "${2}") ;;
01925:         "")     ;;
01926:         *)      echo "usage: raofflineproxy-ctl refresh [--all|--game <id>]" >&2; exit ${EX_USAGE} ;;
01927:     esac
01928:     refuse_unless_ready refresh
01929:     if ! is_online; then
01930:         say "refresh: refused, this device is offline"
01931:         tell "why NO_NETWORK"
01932:         exit ${EX_UNAVAILABLE}
01933:     fi
01934:     # As images: the pid in the lock, a TERM trap over the helper, the
01935:     # verb in RUN_ROUTE (audit #258 PL-013).
01936:     trap 'stopped refresh' TERM
01937:     RUN_ROUTE=refresh
01938:     take_lock refresh
01939:     mark_running
01940:     trap 'unmark_running; [ -n "${CLIENT:-}" ] && kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
01941:     local RC=0
01942:     # The helper looks at its --seconds between games; a game's requests
01943:     # can block past it, so the process is bounded too, a minute's grace
01944:     # past the helper's own ceiling (#308 F-RA-10).
01945:     timeout "$(( TOPUP_TIMEOUT + 60 ))" "${REFRESH_HELPER}" --seconds "${TOPUP_TIMEOUT}" "${WHICH[@]}" &
01946:     CLIENT=$!
01947:     wait "${CLIENT}" || RC=$?
01948:     CLIENT=""
01949:     slog "refresh: rc=${RC} ${WHICH[*]}"
01950:     exit "${RC}"
01951: }
01952: 
01953: do_scan() {
01954:     trap 'stopped scan' TERM
01955:     trap 'cancelled scan' INT
01956:     RUN_ROUTE=scan
01957:     take_lock scan
01958:     refuse_unless_ready scan
01959:     mkdir -p "${PROXY_DIR}" || fail "cannot create ${PROXY_DIR}"
01960:     if ! is_online; then
01961:         say "scan: refused, RetroAchievements is not reachable"
01962:         slog "scan refused: offline by the proxy's probe"
01963:         exit ${EX_UNAVAILABLE}
01964:     fi
01965: 
01966:     local LIST
01967:     LIST="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-scan.XXXXXX)" || fail "cannot create the list"
01968:     # Everything of the run's goes when the run does, however it ends.
01969:     trap 'rm -f "${LIST}" "${JOBS_FIFO:-}" "${READY_BEFORE:-}" "${READY_AFTER:-}" "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next" "${RUNNING}" "${RUNNING}.tmp"; [ -n "${CLIENT:-}" ] && kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
01970: 
01971:     local COUNTS
01972:     R_IMAGES_WHY=""
01973:     mark_running
01974:     tell "doing listing"
01975:     if ! COUNTS="$(list_jobs "${LIST}" all 0 2>>"${SCAN_LOG}")"; then
01976:         slog "scan: the library could not be listed"
01977:         tell "why LIBRARY_UNREADABLE"
01978:         write_stamp 1 scan 0 0 "$(count_ready)" 0 0 0 LIBRARY_UNREADABLE
01979:         exit 1
01980:     fi
01981:     local FOUND NEW TRUNC
01982:     FOUND="$(count_of "${COUNTS}" found)"
01983:     NEW="$(count_of "${COUNTS}" new)"
01984:     TRUNC="$(count_of "${COUNTS}" truncated)"
01985:     slog "scan start: ${COUNTS}"
01986:     if [ "${TRUNC}" -eq 1 ]; then
01987:         slog "scan: the walk stopped at the client's cap of files per run; the next scan walks on from ${SCAN_CURSOR}"
01988:     fi
01989: 
01990:     local READY
01991:     if [ "${FOUND}" -eq 0 ]; then
01992:         # Nothing under the ROM folders to look at is a run that completed
01993:         # with nothing to do, not one that could not finish (fork #329: the
01994:         # page read COULDN'T FINISH on a device with no game yet, and the
01995:         # maintainer's reading was that "there was just nothing to scan").
01996:         # rc 0 and no why; the note tells the page and the stamp what there
01997:         # was to say, and the row reads NO GAMES TO SCAN YET.
01998:         READY="$(count_ready)"
01999:         slog "scan done: no games found under ${ROMS_ROOT}, ready=${READY}"
02000:         tell "note NO_GAMES"
02001:         commit_cursor || slog "scan: an old cursor could not be removed; the next walk starts from the top all the same"
02002:         write_stamp 0 scan 0 0 "${READY}" 0 0 0 "" "" 0 NO_GAMES
02003:         tell "done 0|0|${READY}|0"
02004:         exit 0
02005:     fi
02006:     tell "total ${NEW}"
02007:     if [ "${NEW}" -eq 0 ]; then
02008:         tell "note NOTHING_NEW"
02009:         commit_cursor || slog "scan: an old cursor could not be removed; the next walk starts from the top all the same"
02010:         # No game to cache, but the images of what is cached may still be
02011:         # missing -- a pass the last run cut, a badge that did not come --
02012:         # and pressing SCAN again is how a player asks for them (#307
02013:         # PL-060). The same pass, the same verdict.
02014:         run_image_pass scan "${IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS}"
02015:         READY="$(count_ready)"
02016:         local RC0=0 WHY0="${R_IMAGES_WHY}"
02017:         [ -n "${WHY0}" ] && { RC0=1; tell "why ${WHY0}"; }
02018:         slog "scan done: nothing new, ready=${READY}${WHY0:+ why=${WHY0}}"
02019:         write_stamp "${RC0}" scan 0 0 "${READY}" 0 0 0 "${WHY0}"
02020:         tell "done 0|0|${READY}|0"
02021:         exit "${RC0}"
02022:     fi
02023: 
02024:     READY_BEFORE="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-ready.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null)" && { ready_games_into "${READY_BEFORE}" || { rm -f "${READY_BEFORE}"; READY_BEFORE=""; }; }
02025:     run_jobs page "${LIST}" "${NEW}" 0
02026: 
02027:     READY="$(count_ready)"
02028:     local ADDED=""
02029:     READY_AFTER="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-ready.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null)" && ready_games_into "${READY_AFTER}" && ADDED="$(games_made_ready "${READY_BEFORE}" "${READY_AFTER}")"
02030:     rm -f "${READY_BEFORE}" "${READY_AFTER}"; READY_BEFORE=""; READY_AFTER=""
02031:     # A measurement that failed is said as one (added_count, PL-031).
02032:     ADDED="$(added_count "${ADDED}" "${R_CACHED}")"
02033:     [ "${ADDED}" = "unknown" ] && slog "scan: the store could not be read before or after the jobs; how many games they made ready is not known (added=unknown)"
02034:     local RC=0 WHY="${R_WHY}"
02035:     if [ -n "${WHY}" ]; then
02036:         RC=1
02037:     elif [ "${R_STOPPED}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${R_CLIENT_RC}" -ne 0 ] && [ "${R_DONE}" -eq 0 ]; then
02038:         # The helper died on its own, before its DONE, without a reason the
02039:         # lines above named: the log has its traceback. (After DONE the games
02040:         # are cached and the exit is the badge downloads', fork #188.)
02041:         RC=1; WHY=SOMETHING_WENT_WRONG
02042:     elif [ "${R_ERRORS}" -gt 0 ]; then
02043:         # A fetch that failed for any game, even between games that went
02044:         # through, is a run that did not finish (D-UI-030: a run whose
02045:         # parts disagree is COULDN'T FINISH); the next run tries them again.
02046:         RC=1; WHY=SOME_GAMES_NOT_SAVED
02047:     fi
02048:     # The images of what this run cached, and of anything cached before it
02049:     # that is still missing one (#212): the same action, finished.
02050:     # The scan has no deadline of its own (the top-up's TOPUP_TIMEOUT is the
02051:     # one clock here), so the pass gets its own ceiling.
02052:     # Whenever the run worked through its jobs -- cached one or not: a
02053:     # library with a ROM RetroAchievements does not know lists a job at
02054:     # every scan, and gating the pass on a cached game left such a scan
02055:     # COMPLETED over badges it never looked at (audit of the fixes, claude
02056:     # G-D-02 = gpt G-D-01). Not after a stop on a refused sign-in or a
02057:     # server that stopped answering.
02058:     [ "${R_STOPPED}" -eq 0 ] && run_image_pass scan "${IMAGE_PASS_SECONDS}"
02059:     # The games' own why comes first; a pass that left images behind is the
02060:     # run's why when the games went through (#307 PL-060).
02061:     if [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ -n "${R_IMAGES_WHY}" ]; then
02062:         RC=1; WHY="${R_IMAGES_WHY}"
02063:     fi
02064: 
02065:     # The walk's cursor is kept once the run has worked through its jobs; a
02066:     # run stopped short leaves it where it was (claude G-D-06). A cut walk
02067:     # whose cursor could not be kept promises no continuation: the run could
02068:     # not finish, and neither the page nor the stamp says TRUNCATED (gpt
02069:     # G-D-06).
02070:     if [ "${R_DONE}" -eq 1 ] && [ "${R_STOPPED}" -eq 0 ]; then
02071:         if [ "${TRUNC}" -eq 1 ]; then
02072:             if [ "$(count_of "${COUNTS}" cursor_saved)" -ne 1 ] || ! commit_cursor; then
02073:                 slog "scan: the walk's cursor could not be saved; the next scan would take the same slice"
02074:                 TRUNC=0
02075:                 [ -z "${WHY}" ] && { RC=1; WHY=SOMETHING_WENT_WRONG; }
02076:             fi
02077:         else
02078:             commit_cursor || slog "scan: an old cursor could not be removed; the next walk starts from the top all the same"
02079:         fi
02080:     elif [ "${TRUNC}" -eq 1 ]; then
02081:         slog "scan: the run stopped short of its jobs; the cursor stays where it was"
02082:     fi
02083:     rm -f "${SCAN_CURSOR}.next"
02084:     [ "${R_LIMIT}" -eq 1 ] && tell "note LIMIT_REACHED"
02085:     # Not every folder was walked: the page says so (GuiOfflineScan's
02086:     # NOT EVERY FOLDER WAS LOOKED AT. SCAN AGAIN TO CONTINUE.) and the stamp
02087:     # carries it -- the log alone said it before (#307 PL-059).
02088:     [ "${TRUNC}" -eq 1 ] && tell "note TRUNCATED"
02089:     [ "${R_ERRORS}" -gt 0 ] && tell "errors ${R_ERRORS}"
02090:     [ -n "${WHY}" ] && tell "why ${WHY}"
02091:     write_stamp "${RC}" scan "${R_CACHED}" "${R_SKIPPED}" "${READY}" "${R_LIMIT}" "${R_INDEXED}" "${R_ERRORS}" "${WHY}" "${ADDED}" "${TRUNC}"
02092:     slog "scan done: rc=${RC} cached=${R_CACHED} indexed=${R_INDEXED} skipped=${R_SKIPPED} errors=${R_ERRORS} ready=${READY} limit=${R_LIMIT}${WHY:+ why=${WHY}}"
02093:     say "scan: cached ${R_CACHED} (${R_INDEXED} from the index), skipped ${R_SKIPPED}, ${READY} ready${WHY:+; ${WHY}}"
02094:     tell "done ${R_CACHED}|${R_SKIPPED}|${READY}|${R_LIMIT}"
02095:     exit "${RC}"
02096: }
02097: 
02098: # index-offline: the interface's index had games to identify and
02099: # RetroAchievements' hash library did not come -- offline, nearly always
02100: # (fork #299, D-UI-104). The marker the after-index run leaves when its
02101: # probe fails is written here without a probe, since the interface already
02102: # knows the library did not come: the next link-return topup lists the
02103: # library once, inside the half hour or not, and clears it once that
02104: # listing's games are handled. The games this index could not identify are
02105: # not among them -- they have no cheevosId until an index with the library
02106: # gives them one; the interface runs that index when the link comes up, and
02107: # its topup --after-index caches them (#308 F-RA-22). Nothing else is
02108: # touched; exit 0.
02109: # index-pending holds a token -- when it was written and by which process --
02110: # so a top-up can tell the marker its listing was made for from a newer one
02111: # an index writes while it runs (audit of the fixes, gpt G-D-03). Whole or
02112: # not at all. A marker an earlier build left is an empty file, and reads as
02113: # one token like any other.
02114: #
02115: # The marker has a lock of its own (audit of the fix round, gpt G2-D-03):
02116: # the top-up's token check and its removal are one step under it
02117: # (ack_index_pending), and a write takes it too, so an index's newer marker
02118: # cannot land between that check and that removal and go with the older
02119: # one. It is held for a read, a rename or an unlink, never across anything
02120: # that waits. Busybox flock has no -w: five tries a second apart. A lock
02121: # that cannot be had leaves the safe side -- the write goes ahead, since a
02122: # notification lost leaves the player's games uncached, and the removal
02123: # does not, since a marker kept costs one more listing.
02124: PENDING_LOCK="/var/run/raofflineproxy-index-pending.lock"
02125: pending_lock() {
02126:     local TRY=0
02127:     exec 6<>"${PENDING_LOCK}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
02128:     until flock -n 6; do
02129:         TRY=$((TRY + 1))
02130:         if [ "${TRY}" -ge 5 ]; then exec 6>&-; return 1; fi
02131:         sleep 1
02132:     done
02133: }
02134: 
02135: pending_unlock() {
02136:     exec 6>&-
02137: }
02138: 
02139: write_index_pending() {
02140:     local LOCKED=0 RC=0
02141:     if pending_lock; then LOCKED=1; else say "index-pending: its lock could not be had; written without it"; fi
02142:     printf '%s %s %s\n' "$(date +%s)" "$$" "${RANDOM}" > "${INDEX_PENDING}.tmp" 2>/dev/null \
02143:         && mv -f "${INDEX_PENDING}.tmp" "${INDEX_PENDING}" || RC=1
02144:     [ "${LOCKED}" -eq 1 ] && pending_unlock
02145:     return "${RC}"
02146: }
02147: 
02148: # ack_index_pending <token>: remove index-pending if it is still the marker
02149: # the caller's listing was made for. 0 removed, 1 kept (a newer marker), 2
02150: # kept because the lock could not be had.
02151: ack_index_pending() {
02152:     # Taken aside by rename before it is read: a writer that could not have
02153:     # the lock renames a newer marker into place (write_index_pending's
02154:     # fallback), and a compare-then-rm on the shared path removed that newer
02155:     # one (the audit of the fixes, gpt G3-D-03). Whatever lands on the path
02156:     # after the rename is somebody else's and stays; a moved marker that is
02157:     # not the caller's token goes back.
02158:     local RC=1 mine="${INDEX_PENDING}.ack.$$"
02159:     pending_lock || return 2
02160:     if mv -f "${INDEX_PENDING}" "${mine}" 2>/dev/null; then
02161:         if [ "$(cat "${mine}" 2>/dev/null)" = "${1}" ]; then
02162:             rm -f "${mine}" && [ ! -e "${mine}" ] && RC=0
02163:         else
02164:             [ -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ] || mv -f "${mine}" "${INDEX_PENDING}" 2>/dev/null
02165:             rm -f "${mine}" 2>/dev/null
02166:         fi
02167:     fi
02168:     pending_unlock
02169:     return "${RC}"
02170: }
02171: 
02172: do_index_offline() {
02173:     mkdir -p "${PROXY_DIR}" || fail "cannot create ${PROXY_DIR}"
02174:     write_index_pending || fail "cannot write ${INDEX_PENDING}"
02175:     slog "index ran offline: the hash library did not come (index-pending); the library is listed once at the link's return"
02176: }
02177: 
02178: # topup [--after-index]. --after-index is the run the interface starts as
02179: # its hasher finishes (ThreadedHasher, with the toggle on): it waits for a
02180: # top-up already running instead of giving way to it, and it does not count
02181: # the half-hour since the last attempt against itself -- the index has just
02182: # grown, and that is the one moment a top-up is sure to have something to
02183: # do. It marks the attempt like any other, once its probe has answered.
02184: do_topup() {
02185:     local AFTER_INDEX=0 AI_NOTE=""
02186:     RUN_ROUTE=topup
02187:     if [ "${1:-}" = "--after-index" ]; then AFTER_INDEX=1; AI_NOTE=" (after the index)"; fi
02188:     trap 'stopped topup' TERM
02189:     # One deadline, taken before anything can wait: the lock, the probes,
02190:     # the listing and both passes all spend from it, so the run ends within
02191:     # TOPUP_TIMEOUT of this moment whatever each part costs (#186 PL-28).
02192:     local START
02193:     START="$(date +%s)"
02194:     take_lock topup "${AFTER_INDEX}" "${START}"
02195:     refuse_unless_ready topup >/dev/null
02196:     mkdir -p "${PROXY_DIR}" || fail "cannot create ${PROXY_DIR}"
02197: 
02198:     # Bounded: one attempt per interval, whatever the link does. The mark
02199:     # is read here and set only below, once a probe has reached the server.
02200:     # An index that ran offline (index-pending, below) is the one reason to
02201:     # run inside the interval: the player added games and the toast said
02202:     # they are looked up next time the device is connected (fork #299,
02203:     # D-UI-104), and "next time" is this link, not the one after the half
02204:     # hour. Only a marker written since the last attempt: one a failed
02205:     # attempt left behind (#307 PL-055, below) waits out the half hour like
02206:     # any other run, so a link that flaps does not turn it into a request
02207:     # storm.
02208:     local PENDING_DUE=0
02209:     if [ -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ] && { [ ! -e "${TOPUP_MARK}" ] || [ "${INDEX_PENDING}" -nt "${TOPUP_MARK}" ]; }; then
02210:         PENDING_DUE=1
02211:     fi
02212:     if [ "${AFTER_INDEX}" -eq 0 ] && [ -e "${TOPUP_MARK}" ] && [ "${PENDING_DUE}" -eq 0 ]; then
02213:         local AGE=$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${TOPUP_MARK}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
02214:         if [ "${AGE}" -ge 0 ] && [ "${AGE}" -lt "${TOPUP_INTERVAL}" ]; then
02215:             exit 0
02216:         fi
02217:         # The link's return has one question -- was a game played since the
02218:         # last attempt? -- and no game means nothing to look for: out before
02219:         # the probe, the mark untouched (fork #299, D-RA-035: the maintainer,
02220:         # a nine-second check at wake with nothing to add).
02221:         local HIST
02222:         HIST="$(history_path)"
02223:         if [ ! -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ] && { [ ! -e "${HIST}" ] || [ ! "${HIST}" -nt "${TOPUP_MARK}" ]; }; then
02224:             slog "topup: no game played since the last attempt (${HIST} is not newer than the mark); nothing to look for, skipped"
02225:             exit 0
02226:         fi
02227:     fi
02228: 
02229:     # The hook fires when the address arrives, which can be well before the
02230:     # resolver answers (fork #175: 20-45 s behind on that boot shape), so
02231:     # the probe gets the token check's patience -- PROBE_TRIES tries,
02232:     # PROBE_INTERVAL apart, inside the deadline. A probe that never reached
02233:     # RetroAchievements is not an attempt: no mark, so the next link event
02234:     # (or the after-index run) tries again rather than waiting out the half
02235:     # hour on a connect that was never tested (#186 PL-04).
02236:     local TRY=0 ONLINE=0
02237:     while [ "${TRY}" -lt "${PROBE_TRIES}" ]; do
02238:         TRY=$((TRY + 1))
02239:         if is_online; then ONLINE=1; break; fi
02240:         [ "${TRY}" -lt "${PROBE_TRIES}" ] || break
02241:         [ "$(time_left "${START}")" -gt "${PROBE_INTERVAL}" ] || break
02242:         pause "${PROBE_INTERVAL}"
02243:     done
02244:     if [ "${ONLINE}" -eq 0 ]; then
02245:         slog "topup refused: offline by the proxy's probe (${TRY} probes); not counted as an attempt"
02246:         if [ "${AFTER_INDEX}" -eq 1 ]; then
02247:             write_index_pending
02248:             slog "topup: the index's games wait for the link (index-pending)"
02249:         fi
02250:         exit ${EX_UNAVAILABLE}
02251:     fi
02252:     touch "${TOPUP_MARK}"
02253: 
02254:     local LIST
02255:     LIST="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-topup.XXXXXX)" || fail "cannot create the list"
02256:     trap 'rm -f "${LIST}" "${JOBS_FIFO:-}" "${SC_OUT:-}" "${READY_BEFORE:-}" "${READY_AFTER:-}" "${RUNNING}" "${RUNNING}.tmp"; [ -n "${CLIENT:-}" ] && kill "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
02257:     mark_running
02258:     # The games ready for this account before either pass, for added=.
02259:     READY_BEFORE="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-ready.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null)" && { ready_games_into "${READY_BEFORE}" || { rm -f "${READY_BEFORE}"; READY_BEFORE=""; }; }
02260: 
02261:     # First, every game the interface's index knows and the client has not
02262:     # cached -- the games added and indexed since the last run, and with a
02263:     # library nobody scanned, as many as the deadline allows (the rest next
02264:     # time). Nothing is hashed here.
02265:     local COUNTS LRC NEW=0 CACHED=0 SKIPPED=0 INDEXED=0 LIMIT=0 ERRORS=0 WHY="" LEFT ADDED="" LISTED=0 LIST_WHY=""
02266:     local PENDING_SEEN=0 PENDING_TOKEN=""
02267:     LEFT="$(time_left "${START}")"
02268:     if [ "${LEFT}" -le 0 ]; then
02269:         WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG
02270:         slog "topup${AI_NOTE}: the deadline passed while waiting for the lock and the probe"
02271:     elif [ "${AFTER_INDEX}" -eq 0 ] && [ ! -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ]; then
02272:         # New games are the index's to find -- at startup and with UPDATE
02273:         # GAMELISTS, both of which end in this run with --after-index -- so
02274:         # the link's return does not list the library (fork #299, D-RA-035),
02275:         # unless an index ran offline and left its marker: then once, below.
02276:         slog "topup at the link's return: the recently played pass alone (new games are the index's)"
02277:     else
02278:         # The marker stays until the listing it stands for, and the games
02279:         # that listing found, have been handled -- removed below, never
02280:         # here: a listing that failed, a run cut by the deadline or stopped
02281:         # part-way (STOP IT AND PLAY, disable), a game whose fetch failed,
02282:         # each left no marker and so no retry (#307 PL-055).
02283:         if [ "${AFTER_INDEX}" -eq 0 ]; then
02284:             slog "topup at the link's return: an index ran offline (index-pending); the library listed once for it -- again after the half hour if this run does not finish"
02285:         fi
02286:         # The marker this listing answers, as it reads now: one written
02287:         # after this moment is a newer promise, and stays (gpt G-D-03).
02288:         if [ -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ]; then PENDING_SEEN=1; PENDING_TOKEN="$(cat "${INDEX_PENDING}" 2>/dev/null)"; fi
02289:         COUNTS="$(list_jobs "${LIST}" indexed "${LEFT}" 2>>"${SCAN_LOG}")"
02290:         LRC=$?
02291:         if [ "${LRC}" -eq 0 ]; then
02292:             LISTED=1
02293:             NEW="$(count_of "${COUNTS}" new)"
02294:             slog "topup start${AI_NOTE}: ${COUNTS}"
02295:         elif [ "${LRC}" -eq 124 ]; then
02296:             WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG
02297:             slog "topup${AI_NOTE}: the listing did not finish inside the deadline"
02298:         else
02299:             # The recently played pass still runs -- it needs no index -- but
02300:             # a run a part of which failed is one that could not finish
02301:             # (D-UI-030): the why is kept for the stamp below (audit of the
02302:             # fixes, claude G-D-13; it read COMPLETED before).
02303:             slog "topup${AI_NOTE}: the interface's index could not be read; the recently played pass runs alone"
02304:             LIST_WHY=LIBRARY_UNREADABLE
02305:         fi
02306:     fi
02307:     if [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ "${NEW}" -gt 0 ]; then
02308:         LEFT="$(time_left "${START}")"
02309:         if [ "${LEFT}" -le 0 ]; then
02310:             WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG
02311:         else
02312:             run_jobs quiet "${LIST}" "${NEW}" "${LEFT}"
02313:             CACHED="${R_CACHED}"; SKIPPED="${R_SKIPPED}"; INDEXED="${R_INDEXED}"; LIMIT="${R_LIMIT}"; ERRORS="${R_ERRORS}"; WHY="${R_WHY}"
02314:             # A helper killed by the bound after its DONE finished its games
02315:             # (fork #188: badge downloads kept it alive); only one cut before
02316:             # DONE makes the run one that did not finish.
02317:             if [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ "${R_STOPPED}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${R_CLIENT_RC}" -ne 0 ] && [ "${R_DONE}" -eq 0 ]; then
02318:                 WHY=RETROACHIEVEMENTS_STOPPED_ANSWERING
02319:                 [ "${R_CLIENT_RC}" -eq 124 ] && WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG
02320:             fi
02321:             # As in scan: a game whose fetch failed is a run that did not
02322:             # finish, and the next top-up tries it again (#186 PL-24).
02323:             [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ "${ERRORS}" -gt 0 ] && WHY=SOME_GAMES_NOT_SAVED
02324:             slog "topup indexed pass: cached=${CACHED} indexed=${INDEXED} skipped=${SKIPPED} errors=${ERRORS} rc=${R_CLIENT_RC}${WHY:+ why=${WHY}}"
02325:         fi
02326:     fi
02327: 
02328:     # The index's games are handled -- listed, and each cached or passed
02329:     # over -- so whatever index-pending stood for is done; after-index runs
02330:     # included, since their listing is the same (#307 PL-055).
02331:     # The check and the removal are one step under the marker's lock
02332:     # (ack_index_pending, gpt G2-D-03).
02333:     if [ "${LISTED}" -eq 1 ] && [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ -e "${INDEX_PENDING}" ]; then
02334:         local ACK=1
02335:         [ "${PENDING_SEEN}" -eq 1 ] && { ack_index_pending "${PENDING_TOKEN}"; ACK=$?; }
02336:         case "${ACK}" in
02337:             0) slog "topup: the pending index's listing and its games are handled; index-pending removed" ;;
02338:             1) slog "topup: an index left index-pending while this run was at its jobs; kept for the next run" ;;
02339:             *) slog "topup: index-pending's lock could not be had; the marker is kept and the next run lists for it again" ;;
02340:         esac
02341:     fi
02342: 
02343:     # Then the client's own recently-played pass for what the index missed
02344:     # -- RetroArch's history, PPSSPP's recent list -- each not yet cached,
02345:     # with the client's own pause between requests, in what is left of the
02346:     # deadline. Its progress lines are JSON; the last line is the result.
02347:     # Run in the background and waited for, so a stop request (disable)
02348:     # reaches this process at once and its EXIT trap ends the client.
02349:     LEFT="$(time_left "${START}")"
02350:     if [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ "${LEFT}" -ge 60 ]; then
02351:         local SRC RESULT
02352:         SC_OUT="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-topup-sc.XXXXXX)" || fail "cannot create the result file"
02353:         mark_running
02354:         timeout "${LEFT}" ${PROXY_PY} run-smart-cache > "${SC_OUT}" 2>>"${SCAN_LOG}" &
02355:         CLIENT=$!
02356:         wait "${CLIENT}" 2>/dev/null
02357:         SRC=$?
02358:         unset CLIENT
02359:         unmark_running
02360:         RESULT="$(grep '"type":"result"' "${SC_OUT}" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
02361:         rm -f "${SC_OUT}"; SC_OUT=""
02362:         local SC=0 SS=0 SL=0
02363:         if [ -n "${RESULT}" ]; then
02364:             read -r SC SS SL < <(python3 -c '
02365: import json, sys
02366: r = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
02367: print(int(r.get("cached", 0)), int(r.get("skipped", 0)), 1 if r.get("limit_reached") else 0)
02368: ' "${RESULT}" 2>/dev/null || echo "0 0 0")
02369:         fi
02370:         CACHED=$((CACHED + SC)); SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED + SS)); [ "${SL}" -eq 1 ] && LIMIT=1
02371:         slog "topup recently played: rc=${SRC} cached=${SC} skipped=${SS} limit=${SL}"
02372:         if [ "${SRC}" -ne 0 ]; then
02373:             WHY=RETROACHIEVEMENTS_STOPPED_ANSWERING
02374:             [ "${SRC}" -eq 124 ] && WHY=TOOK_TOO_LONG
02375:         fi
02376:     elif [ -z "${WHY}" ]; then
02377:         slog "topup: no time left for the recently played pass (${LEFT}s)"
02378:     fi
02379: 
02380:     # A listing that could not be read is the run's why when nothing later
02381:     # had one of its own.
02382:     [ -z "${WHY}" ] && [ -n "${LIST_WHY}" ] && WHY="${LIST_WHY}"
02383:     local READY MADE
02384:     READY="$(count_ready)"
02385:     # added=: the games the two passes made ready for this account, from the
02386:     # store before and after (#308 F-RA-10, F-RA-15); unknown when the store
02387:     # could not be read, never the passes' cache operations in its place
02388:     # (added_count, PL-031).
02389:     READY_AFTER="$(mktemp /tmp/raofflineproxy-ready.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null)" && ready_games_into "${READY_AFTER}" && MADE="$(games_made_ready "${READY_BEFORE}" "${READY_AFTER}")" && ADDED="${MADE}"
02390:     rm -f "${READY_BEFORE}" "${READY_AFTER}"; READY_BEFORE=""; READY_AFTER=""
02391:     ADDED="$(added_count "${ADDED}" "${CACHED}")"
02392:     [ "${ADDED}" = "unknown" ] && slog "topup${AI_NOTE}: the store could not be read before or after the passes; how many games they made ready is not known (added=unknown)"
02393:     slog "topup done: cached=${CACHED} added=${ADDED} indexed=${INDEXED} skipped=${SKIPPED} errors=${ERRORS} ready=${READY} limit=${LIMIT} took=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))s${WHY:+ why=${WHY}}"
02394: 
02395:     # The line under the row changes only when the top-up has something to
02396:     # say: games it added, or a run that could not finish. Nothing new
02397:     # leaves the last scan's line as it was.
02398:     if [ -n "${WHY}" ]; then
02399:         write_stamp 1 topup "${CACHED}" "${SKIPPED}" "${READY}" "${LIMIT}" "${INDEXED}" "${ERRORS}" "${WHY}" "${ADDED}"
02400:         say "topup could not finish (${WHY}); cached ${CACHED}, ${READY} ready"
02401:         exit 1
02402:     fi
02403:     if [ "${CACHED}" -gt 0 ]; then
02404:         # The top-up is the background run, so it is where the store is
02405:         # verified as well as filled: a slice per run from the cursor, so
02406:         # the whole store comes round without any one run being long (#213).
02407:         run_image_pass topup "$(time_left "${START}")" --verify
02408:         if [ -n "${R_IMAGES_WHY}" ]; then
02409:             # The games are cached; their images are not all there (#307
02410:             # PL-060): a run whose parts disagree could not finish.
02411:             write_stamp 1 topup "${CACHED}" "${SKIPPED}" "${READY}" "${LIMIT}" "${INDEXED}" "${ERRORS}" "${R_IMAGES_WHY}" "${ADDED}"
02412:             say "topup could not finish (${R_IMAGES_WHY}); cached ${CACHED}, ${READY} ready"
02413:             exit 1
02414:         fi
02415:         write_stamp 0 topup "${CACHED}" "${SKIPPED}" "${READY}" "${LIMIT}" "${INDEXED}" "${ERRORS}" "" "${ADDED}"
02416:         say "topup: cached ${CACHED} game(s), ${INDEXED} from the index; ${READY} ready"
02417:     fi
02418:     exit 0
02419: }
02420: 
02421: case "${1:-}" in
02422:     enable)  do_enable ;;
02423:     disable) do_disable ;;
02424:     start)   do_start ;;
02425:     stop)    do_stop ;;
02426:     status)  do_status ;;
02427:     pending) do_pending ;;
02428:     pending-ids) do_pending_ids ;;
02429:     account) do_account ;;
02430:     summary) do_summary ;;
02431:     flushed) do_flushed ;;
02432:     scan)    do_scan ;;
02433:     topup)   do_topup "${2:-}" ;;
02434:     index-offline) do_index_offline ;;
02435:     ready)   do_ready ;;
02436:     listening) do_listening "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
02437:     images)  do_images "${2:-}" ;;
02438:     refresh) do_refresh "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
02439:     *)
02440:         echo "Usage: raofflineproxy-ctl {enable|disable|start|stop|status|pending|pending-ids|account|summary|flushed|scan|topup [--after-index]|index-offline|images [--verify]|refresh [--all|--game <id>]|listening [--wait <seconds>]|ready}" >&2
02441:         exit 2
02442:     ;;
02443: esac
```

```text
00001: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
00002: # Copyright (C) 2021-present Xargon (https://github.com/XargonWan)
00003: # Copyright (C) 2023 JELOS (https://github.com/JustEnoughLinuxOS)
00004: # Copyright (C) 2025 ROCKNIX Team (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
00005: 
00006: PKG_NAME="rclone"
00007: PKG_VERSION="1.75.2"
00008: # Primary project; embedded dependencies retain their own terms (#528).
00009: PKG_LICENSE="MIT"
00010: # Python3 is the interpreter for cloud_remote. A shipped script's tools are
00011: # real dependencies even though nothing links against them: upstream deleted
00012: # packages/compress/zip in a3d0ad0430, nothing referenced it, and backuptool
00013: # lost its archiver silently for months.
00014: # webkitgtk is here because cloud_oauth needs a browser on the device: a
00015: # provider's OAuth redirect goes to localhost, so it only lands somewhere
00016: # useful if the browser is on the same machine as rclone's authorize listener.
00017: # glib-networking is what gives that browser TLS at all.
00018: # jq is cloud_capture's only JSON reader and writer (the save manifest, #21);
00019: # the same policy as Python3 above -- until now it reached the image only
00020: # through virtual/image's own dependency list.
00021: PKG_DEPENDS_TARGET="toolchain fuse rsync qrencode Python3 \
00022:                     webkitgtk cloud-signin-window glib-networking jq"
00023: PKG_LONGDESC="rsync for cloud storage"
00024: PKG_TOOLCHAIN="manual"
00025: 
00026: # Pinned per arch, and pinned to OUR version.
00027: #
00028: # Upstream added PKG_SHA256 for 1.71.0 in e0a68c95bd while this fork is on
00029: # 1.75.2, so a rebase would bring in a hash that cannot match what we download.
00030: # Setting the right ones here makes that merge a no-op instead of a build
00031: # failure whose message names a checksum and not the version behind it.
00032: #
00033: # Verified against downloads.rclone.org/v1.75.2/SHA256SUMS and independent
00034: # archive hashing (#541). Image assembly strips the binary; installed version
00035: # and protocol proof are recorded separately.
00036: case ${ARCH} in
00037:     aarch64)
00038:       RCLONE_ARCH="arm64"
00039:       PKG_SHA256="7e1e8d69654941b7b7df84ee74c5f7fb09cce7d5496947fb7bf16b55ff427d10"
00040:     ;;
00041:     *)
00042:       RCLONE_ARCH="amd64"
00043:       PKG_SHA256="349ac8fba6ff65d6247043f1750cdcb518ec5d500ef91463a10d37c0ccdf3702"
00044:     ;;
00045: esac
00046: 
00047: PKG_URL="https://downloads.rclone.org/v${PKG_VERSION}/rclone-v${PKG_VERSION}-linux-${RCLONE_ARCH}.zip"
00048: PKG_RCLONE="rclone-v${PKG_VERSION}-linux-${RCLONE_ARCH}/rclone"
00049: 
00050: unpack() {
00051:   # Create build directory
00052:   mkdir -p ${PKG_BUILD}
00053:   # Rename the downloaded zip to include architecture for better tracking
00054:   mv ${SOURCES}/rclone/rclone-${PKG_VERSION}.zip ${SOURCES}/rclone/rclone-${PKG_VERSION}-${RCLONE_ARCH}.zip
00055:   # Extract the binary package to the build directory
00056:   unzip ${SOURCES}/rclone/rclone-${PKG_VERSION}-${RCLONE_ARCH}.zip -d ${PKG_BUILD}/
00057:   # Remove downloaded zip files to conserve space
00058:   rm -f ${SOURCES}/rclone/rclone-${PKG_VERSION}*
00059: }
00060: 
00061: makeinstall_target() {
00062:   mkdir -p ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00063:   mkdir -p ${INSTALL}/usr/config/
00064:   cp cloud_backup ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00065:   cp cloud_restore ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00066:   cp cloud_sync_helper ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00067:   cp cloud_setup ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00068:   cp cloud_folder_validate ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00069:   cp cloud_remote ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00070:   cp cloud_connections.py ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00071:   cp cloud_device_id ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00072:   cp cloud_oauth ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00073:   cp cloud_content_restore ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00074:   cp cloud_content_backup ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00075:   cp cloud_content_transfer ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00076:   cp cloud_sync_cleanup_duplicates.sh ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00077:   cp cloud_saves_root ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00078:   cp cloud_capture ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00079:   # cloud_log_scrub: once per device, masks the credentials earlier builds
00080:   # wrote into cloud_sync.log and the interface's es_log*.txt (the audit of
00081:   # the fix round, PL-014); run at boot by autostart/102-cloud-saves.
00082:   cp cloud_log_scrub ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00083:   # cloud_net_ready: what EmulationStation's startup sync asks before it runs
00084:   # the restore/backup pair -- is the network up, and has it stayed up (#103).
00085:   cp cloud_net_ready ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00086:   # cloud_scan: the restore flow's scan page runs it first and offers only
00087:   # what it found (D-CLOUD-156, fork #350); reads under a parent-held lock.
00088:   cp cloud_scan ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00089:   cp rasteratops-settings-archive ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00090:   # No game-end event hook. EmulationStation runs the save sync itself now
00091:   # (FileData::launchGame), so it can show the result on the progress card
00092:   # instead of backgrounding the work into /dev/null where nobody could tell
00093:   # whether it had happened. The hook had no caller but ES, and leaving it
00094:   # installed would start a second concurrent cloud_backup on the same remote.
00095:   cp ${PKG_BUILD}/${PKG_RCLONE} ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/
00096:   chmod 0755 ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/*
00097:   cp cloud_sync-rules.txt ${INSTALL}/usr/config/
00098:   cp cloud_sync.conf ${INSTALL}/usr/config/
00099:   cp cloud_sync.conf.defaults ${INSTALL}/usr/config/
00100:   cp cloud_sync-rules.txt.defaults ${INSTALL}/usr/config/
00101:   chmod 755 ${INSTALL}/usr/bin/rclone
00102:   # No TOOLS entries for cloud backup and restore.
00103:   #
00104:   # These symlinked the scripts into the tools list, so running one dropped
00105:   # the player into a fullscreen console. That was the parity stopgap while
00106:   # cloud sync had no native surface; EmulationStation now has the whole flow
00107:   # -- direction, the three data classes, progress and the last result -- so
00108:   # the console route is a second, worse way to do the same thing, and two
00109:   # paths to one operation is how somebody ends up with a backup missing what
00110:   # they assumed was in it.
00111: }
```

## FILE projects/ROCKNIX/packages/rocknix/sources/scripts/rocknix-info

```text
00001: #!/bin/bash
00002: 
00003: source /etc/profile
00004: 
00005: ### Apply device quirks
00006: if [ -e "/sys/firmware/devicetree/base/model" ]
00007: then
00008:   export QUIRK_DEVICE="$(tr -d '\0' </sys/firmware/devicetree/base/model 2>/dev/null)"
00009: else
00010:   export QUIRK_DEVICE="$(tr -d '\0' </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null) $(tr -d '\0' </sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null)"
00011: fi
00012: export QUIRK_DEVICE="$(echo ${QUIRK_DEVICE} | sed -e "s#[/]#-#g")"
00013: 
00014: info_quirks() {
00015:   local status=0
00016:   for QUIRK in /usr/lib/autostart/quirks/platforms/"${HW_DEVICE}"/info.d/${1}/* \
00017:                /usr/lib/autostart/quirks/devices/"${QUIRK_DEVICE}"/info.d/${1}/*
00018:   do
00019:     [ -f "${QUIRK}" ] && [ -x "${QUIRK}" ] || continue
00020:     "${QUIRK}" 2>/dev/null || status=$?
00021:   done
00022:   return "${status}"
00023: }
00024: 
00025: # Hardware readings are optional (including on GENERIC_X64). Read and validate
00026: # before arithmetic; a missing value is not a measured zero (#548).
00027: info_frequency() {
00028:   local value
00029:   value=$(cat -- "$1" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
00030:   [[ "$value" =~ ^[0-9]{1,18}$ ]] || return 1
00031:   printf '%s' "$((10#$value / $2))"
00032: }
00033: 
00034: info_frequency_label() {
00035:   if [ -n "$1" ]; then
00036:     printf '%s MHz' "$1"
00037:   else
00038:     printf '%s' 'Not Available'
00039:   fi
00040: }
00041: 
00042: info_temperature() {
00043:   local sensor value
00044:   for sensor in "$@"; do
00045:     value=$(cat -- "$sensor" 2>/dev/null) || continue
00046:     [[ "$value" =~ ^-?[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] && printf '%s\n' "$value"
00047:   done | awk '{total += $1; count++} END {if (count) printf "%d", total/count/1000}'
00048: }
00049: 
00050: ### Grab battery capacity now as it is used in a couple of different places
00051: ### Cater for batteryplus
00052: BATTERYPLUS_PERCENT="/tmp/battery.percent"
00053: 
00054: if [[ -f "${BATTERYPLUS_PERCENT}" ]]; then
00055:   BATT=$(<${BATTERYPLUS_PERCENT})

00058: fi
00059: 
00060: ### short version (for osd)
00061: if test "$1" = "--short"
00062: then
00063:     DT=$(date +%H:%M)
00064:     if test -n "${BATT}"
00065:     then
00066: 	echo "Battery: ${BATT}% - ${DT}"
00067:     else
00068: 	echo "${DT}"
00069:     fi
00070:     exit 0
00071: fi
00072: ###
00073: 
00074: V_CPUNB=$(grep -E $'^processor\t:' /proc/cpuinfo | wc -l)
00075: V_CPUMODEL1=$(grep -E $'^model name\t:' /proc/cpuinfo | head -1 | sed -e s+'^model name\t: '++)
00076: V_SYSTEM=$(uname -rs)
00077: V_ARCH=$(uname -m)
00078: 
00079: [[ "$V_CPUMODEL1" ]] || V_CPUMODEL1="${HW_CPU}"
00080: 
00081: # network
00082: ip=$(ip -4 addr show dev eth0 2>/dev/null | grep inet | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d/ -f1)
00083: if [ -z "$ip" ]; then
00084:   WIFI_DEV="$({ ls /sys/class/net; echo wlan0; } | grep -m1 ^wlan)"
00085:   ip=$(ip -4 addr show dev ${WIFI_DEV} 2>/dev/null | grep inet | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d/ -f1)
00086: fi
00087: if [ -z "$ip" ]; then

00090: 
00091: host=$(hostname)
00092: 
00093: # cpu

00096:     CPUMAX=$(info_frequency /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy0/cpuinfo_max_freq 1000)

00108: 
00109: # gpu

00120:

00126: 
00127: # battery
00128: case ${HW_ARCH} in
00129:   aarch64)
00130:     declare -a CF MF
00131: 
00132:     for CPUFREQ in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/*
00133:     do

00135:       then
00136:         continue
00137:       fi
00138:       RELCPUS=$(cat ${CPUFREQ}/related_cpus 2>/dev/null)

00140:       then
00141:         FIELD="$(cat ${CPUFREQ}/related_cpus 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1"-"$NF}')"
00142:       else
00143:         FIELD="$(cat ${CPUFREQ}/related_cpus 2>/dev/null)"
00144:       fi
00145:       if FREQ=$(info_frequency "${CPUFREQ}/scaling_cur_freq" 1000); then
00146:         [ "${#CF[@]}" -gt 0 ] || CF+=("CURRENT FREQUENCY:")
00147:         CF+=("THREADS ${FIELD}: ${FREQ}MHz")
00148:       fi
00149:       if FREQ=$(info_frequency "${CPUFREQ}/scaling_max_freq" 1000); then
00150:         [ "${#MF[@]}" -gt 0 ] || MF+=("MAXIMUM FREQUENCY:")
00151:         MF+=("THREADS ${FIELD}: ${FREQ}MHz")
00152:       fi
00153:     done
00154:   ;;
00155: esac
00156: 
00157: echo "SYSTEM INFORMATION:"
00158: echo "DEVICE: ${QUIRK_DEVICE}"
00159: echo "OPERATING SYSTEM: ${OS_NAME}"
00160: echo "VERSION: ${OS_VERSION}"
00161: if [ -n "${BUILD_TIMESTAMP}" ]; then

00167: if [ -n "${DEVICE_SERIAL_NUMBER_PATH}" ]; then

00169:   if [ -n "${SOC_SERIAL}" ]; then
```

```text
00001: #!/bin/bash
00002: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
00003: # Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
00004: #
00005: # fork-package-freshness -- are the packages this fork introduces at their
00006: # current upstream release?
00007: #
00008: #   tools/fork-package-freshness              # every fork-introduced package
00009: #   tools/fork-package-freshness rclone ...   # only these
00010: #   tools/fork-package-freshness --list       # name the packages and stop
00011: #
00012: # Exit 0 when every package is CURRENT, PINNED on purpose, INHERITED or
00013: # LOCAL; 1 when any is BEHIND; 2 when any could not be checked (UNKNOWN):
00014: # a check that cannot run has not passed (engineering-practices.md).
00015: #
00016: # Which packages: every package.mk on HEAD_REF (next) that is absent on
00017: # BASE_REF (upstream/next) -- the fork added it -- plus EXTRA_PACKAGES,
00018: # recipes the fork owns although upstream carries a copy. Maintainer,
00019: # 2026-09-20 (fork #227, D-WORKFLOW-024): "we should also make sure that
00020: # packages we're introducing into the system are up to date ... it's a good
00021: # idea to have everything as up to date as possible when we submit it."
00022: #
00023: # How "latest" is found, by the host PKG_URL points at:
00024: #   github.com               the latest release, else the newest release-shaped tag
00025: #   codeberg.org             the newest stable version among repository tags
00026: #   download.gnome.org       cache.json, even minor versions only (GNOME stable)
00027: #   ftp.gnu.org / savannah   the directory listing
00028: #   webkitgtk.org            the release listing, even minor versions only
00029: #   cache.ruby-lang.org      ruby/ruby tags in the minor series the recipe names
00030: #                            (# freshness: series X.Y -- <why>), else the version's own
00031: #   downloads.rclone.org     rclone/rclone's latest release
00032: #   dotat.at                 the directory listing, else fanf2/unifdef on GitHub
00033: # A PKG_VERSION that is a commit hash is compared with the default branch of
00034: # the repository PKG_SITE names and reported as commits behind it. A recipe
00035: # that must stay where it is says what it follows:
00036: #   # freshness: pinned -- <why>
00037: # and is reported PINNED. A recipe with no PKG_VERSION of its own sources
00038: # upstream's generic recipe (INHERITED); one with no PKG_URL is ours (LOCAL).
00039: set -uo pipefail
00040: 
00041: ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
00042: HEAD_REF=${FRESHNESS_HEAD:-next}
00043: BASE_REF=${FRESHNESS_BASE:-upstream/next}
00044: EXTRA_PACKAGES="projects/ROCKNIX/packages/network/rclone"
00045: 
00046: var() { grep -m1 "^${2}=" "$1" | cut -d'"' -f2; }
00047: newest() { sort -V | tail -1; }
00048: release_only() { grep -E '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$'; }          # no rc, alpha, beta
00049: tag_version() { sed -E 's/^[^0-9]*//; s/_/./g'; }          # v1.2.0, libpsl-0.21.0, v3_3_12
00050: github_repo() { sed -nE 's#^https?://github\.com/([^/]+/[^/#?]+).*#\1#p' <<<"$1" | sed 's/\.git$//'; }
00051: 
00052: latest_github() {  # <owner/repo>
00053:     local v
00054:     v=$(gh api "repos/$1/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null | tag_version | release_only)
00055:     [ -n "$v" ] && { echo "$v"; return; }
00056:     gh api "repos/$1/tags?per_page=50" --jq '.[].name' 2>/dev/null | tag_version | release_only | newest
00057: }
00058: latest_codeberg() {  # <owner/repo>
00059:     local tags
00060:     tags=$(curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/$1/tags?limit=50" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
00061:     python3 -c 'import json, sys; print("\n".join(tag["name"] for tag in json.load(sys.stdin)))' <<<"$tags" 2>/dev/null \
00062:         | tag_version | release_only | newest
00063: }
00064: latest_gnome() {  # <module>
00065:     curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "https://download.gnome.org/sources/$1/cache.json" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
00066: import json, sys, re
00067: d = json.load(sys.stdin); p = sys.argv[1]
00068: vs = [v for v in d[2].get(p, []) if re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?", v)]
00069: vs = [v for v in vs if int(v.split(".")[1]) % 2 == 0]
00070: vs.sort(key=lambda s: [int(x) for x in s.split(".")])
00071: print(vs[-1] if vs else "")' "$1"
00072: }
00073: latest_listing() {  # <directory url> <name>
00074:     curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "$2-[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+\.tar" | sed -E "s/^$2-//; s/\.tar$//" | newest
00075: }
00076: latest_webkitgtk() {
00077:     curl -fsSL --max-time 30 https://webkitgtk.org/releases/ 2>/dev/null \
00078:         | grep -oE 'webkitgtk-2\.[0-9]*[02468]\.[0-9]+\.tar\.xz' | sed -E 's/^webkitgtk-//; s/\.tar\.xz$//' | newest
00079: }
00080: latest_ruby() {  # <recipe version, or a series X.Y> -- newest in that minor series
00081:     local series=$1
00082:     [[ $series =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] && series=${series%.*}
00083:     gh api "repos/ruby/ruby/tags?per_page=100" --jq '.[].name' 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^v${series//./_}_[0-9]+$" | tag_version | newest
00084: }
00085: commits_behind() {  # <owner/repo> <sha>
00086:     gh api "repos/$1/compare/$2...HEAD" --jq 'if .ahead_by == 0 then "0 behind"
00087:         else "\(.ahead_by) behind \(.commits[-1].sha[0:10]) (\(.commits[-1].commit.committer.date[0:10]))" end' 2>/dev/null
00088: }
00089: packages() {
00090:     # Only build-engine recipe roots; docs/ holds immutable historical fixtures.
00091:     git -C "$ROOT" diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" -- packages projects | sed -n 's|/package.mk$||p'
00092:     for p in $EXTRA_PACKAGES; do echo "$p"; done
00093: }
00094: 
00095: if [ "${1:-}" = "--list" ]; then packages; exit 0; fi
00096: 
00097: rc=0
00098: printf '%-26s %-14s %-14s %s\n' PACKAGE RECIPE LATEST VERDICT
00099: while read -r d; do
00100:     name=$(basename "$d")
00101:     if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then case " $* " in *" $name "*) ;; *) continue ;; esac; fi
00102:     f="$ROOT/$d/package.mk"
00103:     if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then printf '%-26s %-14s %-14s %s\n' "$name" - - "UNKNOWN: no package.mk in the working tree"; rc=2; continue; fi
00104:     ver=$(var "$f" PKG_VERSION); url=$(var "$f" PKG_URL); site=$(var "$f" PKG_SITE)
00105:     pinned=$(grep -m1 -E '^# freshness: pinned -- ' "$f" | sed 's/^# freshness: pinned -- //')
00106:     # A recipe held to a minor series says so in the same place, and the tool
00107:     # follows the recipe rather than carrying the rule itself (audit #258 PL-027).
00108:     series_line=$(grep -m1 -E '^# freshness: series [0-9]+\.[0-9]+ -- ' "$f")
00109:     series=${series_line#\# freshness: series }; series=${series%% -- *}
00110:     series_why=${series_line#* -- }
00111:     [ -n "$series_line" ] || { series=""; series_why=""; }
00112:     latest=""; verdict=""
00113:     if [ -z "$ver" ] && grep -qE '^\. .*/package\.mk' "$f"; then
00114:         verdict="INHERITED"
00115:     elif [ -z "$url" ]; then
00116:         verdict="LOCAL"
00117:     elif [ -z "$ver" ]; then
00118:         verdict="UNKNOWN: PKG_URL without a PKG_VERSION"; rc=2
00119:     elif [[ "$ver" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
00120:         repo=$(github_repo "$site")
00121:         if [ -z "$repo" ]; then
00122:             verdict="UNKNOWN: PKG_SITE is not a GitHub repository"; rc=2
00123:         else
00124:             behind=$(commits_behind "$repo" "$ver"); latest=${behind%% *}
00125:             case "$behind" in
00126:                 "")   verdict="UNKNOWN: compare failed for $repo"; rc=2 ;;
00127:                 0\ *) verdict="CURRENT (the pin is HEAD)" ;;
00128:                 *)    if [ -n "$pinned" ]; then verdict="PINNED: $pinned ($behind)"
00129:                       else verdict="BEHIND: $behind"; [ $rc -lt 1 ] && rc=1; fi ;;
00130:             esac
00131:         fi
00132:     else
00133:         # the recipe's own URL pattern, with its version; variables a recipe sets
00134:         # elsewhere (rclone's RCLONE_ARCH) expand empty, the host survives
00135:         eurl=$( set +u; PKG_VERSION=$ver; PKG_NAME=$name; SOURCEFORGE_SRC=https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project
00136:                 eval "$(grep -E '^PKG_(NAME|SITE)=' "$f")"; eval "$(grep -m1 '^PKG_URL=' "$f")"; echo "$PKG_URL" )
00137:         host=$(sed -E 's#^[a-z]+://([^/]+).*#\1#' <<<"$eurl")
00138:         case "$eurl" in
00139:             https://downloads.rclone.org/*) latest=$(latest_github rclone/rclone) ;;
00140:             *cache.ruby-lang.org/*)         latest=$(latest_ruby "${series:-$ver}") ;;
00141:             *webkitgtk.org/*)               latest=$(latest_webkitgtk) ;;
00142:             *download.gnome.org/sources/*)  latest=$(latest_gnome "$(sed -nE 's#.*/sources/([^/]+)/.*#\1#p' <<<"$eurl")") ;;
00143:             *ftp.gnu.org/gnu/*|*savannah.gnu.org/releases/*)
00144:                                             latest=$(latest_listing "$(dirname "${eurl/#http:/https:}")/" "$name") ;;
00145:             *dotat.at/*)                    latest=$(latest_listing "$(dirname "$eurl")/" "$name")
00146:                                             [ -n "$latest" ] || latest=$(latest_github fanf2/unifdef) ;;   # dotat.at is often down; same author, same tags
00147:             *github.com/*)                  latest=$(latest_github "$(github_repo "$eurl")") ;;
00148:             https://codeberg.org/*)         latest=$(latest_codeberg "$(sed -nE 's#^https://codeberg\.org/([^/]+/[^/]+).*#\1#p' <<<"$eurl")") ;;
00149:         esac
00150:         if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
00151:             if [ -n "$pinned" ]; then verdict="PINNED: $pinned (latest not resolvable)"
00152:             else verdict="UNKNOWN: no resolver for $host, or it did not answer"; rc=2; fi
00153:         elif [ "$latest" = "$ver" ]; then
00154:             verdict="CURRENT"; [ -n "$series" ] && verdict="CURRENT in series $series: $series_why"
00155:         elif [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ver" "$latest" | newest)" = "$latest" ]; then
00156:             if [ -n "$pinned" ]; then verdict="PINNED: $pinned (latest $latest)"
00157:             else verdict="BEHIND"; [ $rc -lt 1 ] && rc=1; fi
00158:         else
00159:             verdict="AHEAD of upstream's latest"
00160:         fi
00161:     fi
00162:     printf '%-26s %-14s %-14s %s\n' "$name" "${ver:0:14}" "${latest:0:14}" "$verdict"
00163: done < <(packages)
00164: exit $rc
```

```text
00023: 289: # Honor the caller's build-drive TMPDIR for the owned host fixture tree.
00024: 290: # Host compilers and patch commands below explicitly use this owned tree too.
00025: 291: # Bubblewrap descendants get a private /tmp, so an inherited host-only path
00026: 292: # makes otherwise valid mktemp calls fail inside the device fixture.
00027: 293: TMP="$(mktemp -d)" || { echo "cannot create host fixture directory" >&2; exit 2; }
00028: 294: trap 'rm -rf "${TMP}"' EXIT
00029: 295: unset TMPDIR
00030: 296: FAIL=0
00031: 297: SKIPPED=0
00032: 298: NOT_APPLICABLE=0
00033: 299: # skip <text>: a check that did not run is counted, never folded into PASSED
00034: 300: # (audit of the fix round PL-023): the verdict says how many, and exits 3
00035: 301: # when nothing failed but something was skipped -- vm-qa reads 3 as SKIP.
00036: 302: skip() { SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED + 1)); echo "    SKIP  $*"; }
00037: 303: # The signal dispositions this run inherited (PL-025): vm-qa's wrapper resets
00038: 304: # SIGINT and SIGPIPE before exec; SigIgn bit 1 is SIGINT, bit 12 SIGPIPE. Read
00039: 305: # from /proc/$$ -- the first cut read /proc/self inside $( ), which is awk's own
00040: 306: # process, and awk reads SIGPIPE ignored where this shell has it default.
00041: 307: sigign="$(awk '/^SigIgn:/{print $2}' "/proc/$$/status")"   # $$ is this script, not the awk
00042: 308: echo "signals: SigIgn=${sigign} SIGINT ignored=$(( (16#${sigign} >> 1) & 1 )) SIGPIPE ignored=$(( (16#${sigign} >> 12) & 1 ))"
00043: 309: check() { # <0|nonzero> ok-text bad-text
00044: 310:     if [ "$1" -eq 0 ]; then echo "    PASS  $2"; else echo "    FAIL  $3"; FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); fi
00045: 311: }

00064: 330:         connection_dir="$(dirname "$2")"
```
